linkedin_detail_4450215119.description: Job description: Job Title: Security Advisor. Company: Sardar Group. Location: Erbil. Overall Objective of the Job: The Security Advisor is responsible for providing strategic and operational security advice to support the organization's corporate operations in Iraq and the Kurdistan Region. The role focuses on safeguarding employees, expatriate staff, assets, information, and business operations through proactive risk management and security planning. The Security Advisor serves as a key focal point for security-related matters, ensuring that security measures are aligned with business objectives while maintaining a safe and secure working environment for all personnel. Tasks and Responsibilities: Security Risk Management Conduct security risk assessments for offices, residences, travel routes, and operational activities. The Security Advisor shall review and evaluate the performance of security guards during both announced and unannounced visits through and in coordination with the Administration dept. Any performance concerns or repeated violations should be reported to the responsible department or security service provider. The Security Advisor shall ensure that each company location maintains an accurate entry and exit logbook, or approved electronic register, for all visitors, contractors, suppliers, employees, and vehicles entering or leaving the premises. This can be achieved in coordination with the location receptionists. Identify emerging threats and vulnerabilities and recommend appropriate mitigation measures. Review and update security risk registers and mitigation plans. Support the development and implementation of security policies, procedures, and standards. Expatriate and Personnel Security Provide security briefings and induction training for expatriate employees, visitors, and consultants. Monitor the security situation affecting expatriate personnel and provide timely advice and guidance. Support residential security assessments and recommend improvements where necessary. Assist in the development and implementation of personnel security measures for high-risk activities. Travel Security Conduct travel risk assessments for domestic and international travel. Monitor travel movements of expatriate personnel and provide security guidance when required. Coordinate travel security arrangements, including route assessments, secure transportation, and contingency planning. Provide security advice regarding travel restrictions, high-risk areas, and emerging threats. Crisis and Incident Management Investigate security incidents and prepare comprehensive reports with recommendations. Maintain incident tracking and ensure corrective actions are implemented. Security Operations Advise/support the management of office security systems, access control measures, and guard force operations. Direct the Administration Department to conduct regular security inspections and audits of company facilities and ensure compliance with established security requirements. The Security Advisor shall ensure that CCTV, access control systems, alarm systems, lighting, barriers, gates, and other physical security systems are functional, properly monitored, and periodically tested. The Security Advisor shall also review CCTV footage when required for investigations, incidents, compliance checks, or management requests. The Security Advisor shall ensure that security guards have the required equipment and tools to perform their duties effectively, including: Uniforms Communication tools Flashlights Logbooks Visitor badges Barriers Emergency contact lists The Security Advisor shall prepare monthly security performance reports covering: Security incidents Site inspections Guard performance Access control compliance CCTV and security system issues Visitor and vehicle logbook findings Open corrective actions Key security risks Guard compliance Measurement: Attendance, uniform, alertness, discipline, and compliance with procedures. Logbook compliance. Measurement: Missing entries, incomplete information, and repeated violations. CCTV and system uptime Measurement: Cameras, access control systems, alarms, and other security systems working properly. Ensure compliance with corporate security standards and local regulatory requirements. Stakeholder Engagement Develop and maintain effective relationships with local authorities, security agencies, landlords, and business partners. Support departmental managers in implementing security requirements within their areas of responsibility. Job Requirements: Based at the corporate office with periodic travel within Iraq and the Kurdistan Region. May require visits to employee residences, project sites, hotels, and other operational locations. Availability to respond to emergencies and security incidents outside normal working hours. Participation in crisis management and business continuity activities when required. Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field. Minimum 8 years of security experience, preferably within corporate, international, diplomatic, oil and gas, or multinational environments. Experience working in Iraq and/or the Kurdistan Region is highly desirable. Strong understanding of the security environment in Iraq and the Kurdistan Region. Knowledge of expatriate security and travel risk management. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, Arabic, and Kurdish. Ability to prepare professional security reports, briefings, and presentations. Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills. High level of integrity, discretion, and confidentiality. Ability to work independently and under pressure in a dynamic environment.

linkedin_detail_4413602602.description: Summary To lead and strengthen our telecom operator’s security posture. The ideal candidate will have deep, hands-on expertise across the entire security stack, combining practical operational skills with theoretical frameworks and industry best practices. This role requires strong technical proficiency, leadership, and the ability to design, implement, and manage advanced security solutions in a fast-paced telecom environment. Key Responsibilities Define and enforce the organization’s information security policies, standards, and frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST, CIS, ITU-T). Conduct risk assessments, gap analyses, and threat modelling specific to telecom infrastructure. Lead incident detection, response, and recovery for telecom networks. Manage SOC/NOC integration, SIEM platforms, IDS/IPS, firewalls, and endpoint security. Conduct penetration testing, red-teaming, and vulnerability assessments. Oversee fraud management and revenue assurance security aspects. Secure telecom-specific technologies (SS7, Diameter, SIP, IMS, VoLTE, 5G/4G networks, MPLS, IoT/M2M). Ensure protecting subscriber privacy. Harden BSS/OSS, mediation, billing, and customer platforms. Secure hybrid cloud (OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, AWS/Azure). Protect customer data (CDRs, subscriber records, financial transactions) using encryption, tokenization, and DLP. Ensure security by design in API, mobile apps, and enterprise applications. Mentor junior engineers, promote security awareness, collaborate with IT, network, legal, and compliance teams, and engage with regulators and auditors. Competencies Advanced knowledge of telecom protocols (SS7, SIP, Diameter, GTP, SCTP). Strong experience with firewalls, IDS/IPS, SIEM, EDR, DLP, WAF, IAM. Expertise in PKI, TLS, IPsec, VPNs, and zero-trust. Proficiency in scripting (Python, Bash, PowerShell). Deep understanding of cryptography, secure architecture, and cyber threat intelligence. Familiarity with telecom fraud scenarios (SIM box, bypass, signalling fraud). Knowledge of regulatory frameworks. Strong analytical skills, excellent communication, and leadership capabilities. CISSP, CISM, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer. CEH, OSCP, GPEN, GCIH, GCIA certificates is preferred. CCSP, Microsoft SC-100, AWS/Azure Security Specialty. 5G Security (ENISA/GSMA) or equivalent. Proven track record of hands-on security implementations and leading security teams. Experience responding to APTs, telecom fraud, and large-scale incidents. Language English (required) Kurdish (preferred) Arabic (preferred) Experience 7-10 years of work experience in relevant field. Education Bachelor or Master in Computer Science, Information Security, Telecommunications, or related field.

Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Organizational Context and Scope IOM Iraq’s PVE program aims at analysing and addressing underlying drivers, motivations and vulnerabilities to violent extremism that may arise in context of marginalization, exclusion, human rights violations, social isolation, exposure to radical ideologies, and lack of livelihood opportunities. monitor progress and report to the Airport Operations Director. • Liaise with the GHS Department, any other ground service providers, airlines, and other airside stakeholders, ensuring alignment with airside regulatory requirements and operational standards. • Develop and monitor airside operational performance metrics, KPIs and service level indicators, ensuring continuous improvement in airside safety and operational efficiency. • Participate in and support the airport committees established by ICAA and/or defined by ICAO, contributing as a subject matter expert on airside operations matters; • Serves as a member of the Airside Operations Department, on the Runway Safety Committee, and Safety and Environmental Committee (if established); • Serves as a member of the EOC and Airport Crisis Management Center; • Advises the Airport Operations Director on various technical/operational airside matters; • Prepares, coordinates and reviews airside-related correspondence with external agencies, regulators and other stakeholders; • Serves as a member of the Airside Operations Department management team and participates in planning for operational matters affecting the department’s activities; Human Resources Management • Promotes and systematically ensures the correct application of all company policies regarding human resources and corporate processes; • Coordinates and ensures the correct management of the tasks and human resources within the subordinate departments and Sections; • Conducts annual performance and competency reviews and ensures that all employees are adequately and properly trained and qualified to perform the assigned duties; • Manages and mobilizes human resources within the subordinate units to support emergency and contingency situations, as required by the Airport Emergency Plan and Security Program. • Ensures distribution and use of required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and monitors and reports all incidents and OHS situations to the Safety Office. • Manages the human resources of the Airside Operations Department and liaises with the Human Resources Department on all personnel matters, namely departmental needs, resignations, absences, disciplinary matters, etc; linkedin_detail_4429703361.description: Who We Are Galaxy is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, delivering solutions that accelerate progress in finance and artificial intelligence. We believe that blockchain and digital asset innovation will transform how value moves through the world – and we’re building the products and services to make that future a reality. Our institutional digital assets platform spans trading, investment banking, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization technology. We also invest in and operate cutting-edge data center infrastructure to power AI and high-performance computing, addressing the growing demand for scalable energy and compute in the U.S. We work at the intersection of finance and technology, helping institutions, startups, and developers navigate a digitally native economy. Led by CEO and Founder Michael Novogratz, our team blends deep crypto expertise with institutional experience and a shared commitment to shaping the future of Web3 and AI. Galaxy is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. To learn more about our businesses and products, visit www.galaxy.com. What We Value We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be. Seek Excellence. Be Selective To Be Effective. Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled. Disagree Transparently. Encourage Independent Decision-Making. Build Dream Teams. Who You Are You'll own the contract and program layer of systems that real institutions depend on — tokenized funds, staking and validator infrastructure, collateral and liquidity products, and the compliance primitives that make them usable inside regulated workflows. This is a builder role with a research dimension. You'll move between protocol-level design work and shipping production contracts that clear institutional audit, security, and operational bars. You own your work end-to-end: spec, contracts, tests, deployment tooling, monitoring, runbooks, and the off-chain integrations that make contracts operable in production. What You’ll Do Design and ship on-chain systems Design, implement, and ship smart contracts and on-chain programs across EVM and Solana for tokenized funds, staking systems, and capital markets primitives. Own contract-level architecture decisions: upgrade paths, access control, transfer restrictions, oracle integration, fee and accounting logic, and failure modes. Work end-to-end on each system — from spec through to deployment tooling, monitoring, runbooks, and the off-chain integrations that make contracts operable in production. Build for regulation institutions Build the compliance and control surfaces that let regulated institutions actually use these systems — KYC/AML enforcement at the protocol layer, role-based access, investor-class restrictions, and auditable mint/burn/transfer flows. Translate ambiguous product or regulatory requirements into concrete contract designs without heavy process. Own security and rigor Drive the security posture of what you ship — threat modelling, invariant and fuzz testing, internal review, and working with external auditors. Contribute to technical research that shapes the next generation of Edge's on-chain products What We’re Looking For 4+ years of production engineering experience, with substantial time spent shipping smart contracts or on-chain programs that handle real value. Deep fluency in at least one of Solidity (Foundry/Hardhat, EVM internals, upgrade patterns) or Solana programs (Rust, Anchor, Token-2022, SPL); credible working knowledge of the other, or a clear track record of picking up new chain ecosystems quickly. Strong instincts for smart contract security — you've thought hard about reentrancy, oracle manipulation, access control, and the failure modes specific to your stack, and you write code that reflects it. Comfort owning systems end-to-end, including the off-chain pieces that production contracts depend on. Ability to operate in a high-autonomy environment. High agency, low ego. You own your work end-to-end and hold yourself accountable for quality. Bonus Points Experience with tokenized assets, regulated financial products, or institutional DeFi. Familiarity with tokenized vault standards (ERC-4626, ERC-7540 for asynchronous deposit/redemption flows) and Token-2022 extensions such as transfer hooks. Background in capital markets, custody, or staking infrastructure. Prior work that has been through formal audit. What We Offer Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus Hybrid/Flexible Working Arrangements Flexible Time Off (paid) 3% 401(k) company contribution Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents Generous paid Parental Leave Competitive family planning benefits for US employees Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues Free daily snacks and weekly breakfasts/lunches Employee Resource Groups Free coaching and counseling sessions through Headspace Apply now and join us on our mission to engineer a new economic paradigm. The base salary ranges included below will be commensurate with candidate experience, expertise and local market. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise. At Galaxy, we maintain a total compensation philosophy which consists of a competitive base salary, annual bonus, and equity incentives. Base Salary Range $200,000 - $250,000 USD Galaxy respects diversity and seeks to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and job applicants for employment without regard to actual or perceived age, race, color, creed, religion

Ecosystem Token Options: Up to a 20% allocation of native $AGS utility protocol tokens. Vesting Protection: Standard 4-year vesting with a 1-to-3 year flexible milestone cliff designed to align perfectly with our early-stage pre-launch ecosystem grants. Total Cash-Out Mechanics: Fully defined liquidity provisions within our private bylaws, allowing clear paths to liquidity upon subsequent venture financing rounds, corporate acquisition, or protocol programmatic token listing events. Requirements: Deep production experience building clean dashboards with Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind . Hands-on history writing/deploying audited Solidity contracts, managing multi-chain transactions via viem/wagmi , and deploying on Base . Familiarity with decentralized data storage abstractions (Arweave via the Irys SDK) and Stripe backend webhook structures.

linkedin_detail_4422121734.description: Who We Are FTI Consulting is the leading global expert firm for organizations facing crisis and transformation. We work with many of the world’s top multinational corporations, law firms, banks and private equity firms on their most important issues to deliver impact that makes a difference. From resolving disputes, navigating crises, managing risk and optimizing performance, our teams respond rapidly to dynamic and complex situations. At FTI Consulting, you’ll work side-by side with leaders who have shaped history, helping solve the biggest challenges making headlines today. From day one, you’ll be an integral part of a focused team where you can make a real impact. You’ll be surrounded by an open, collaborative culture that embraces diversity, recognition, professional development and, most importantly, you. Are you ready to make your impact? About The Role FTI’s Blockchain and Digital Assets practice provides a full range of services across the blockchain and digital assets sectors. Services include bankruptcy and restructuring, M&A due diligence, investigations, strategy and innovation, blockchain as a Service (BaaS), and more. You can learn more about our services by visiting: https://www.ftitechnology.com/solutions/blockchain-and-digital-asset-solutions What You’ll Do Support client engagement teams across investigations and strategy working with a wide variety of clients to deliver professional services, investigative services, expert reports, and support business development activities at a strategic and tactical level. Translate client requirements into formal agreements, establish specific solutions/workflows, and lead the efforts that culminate in client acceptance of the results. Lead in the design, development, and deployment of each client blockchain or digital assets solution, excel at project consulting and management, deliver product selection and implementation, and achieve outstanding implementation results. Responsible for contractual cost estimation, budget adherence, schedule creation, timeline management, and other deliverables. Manage resources and coordinate client resources to deliver services and solutions to support the client organization and the program. Work closely with leadership to significantly contribute to thought-leadership initiatives, go to market strategies, sales efforts, and other practice development activities. How You’ll Grow You’ll work in a team that has over 26 combined specialized cryptocurrency, blockchain, NFT and metaverse certifications and is pioneering the work that is building the future of the decentralized ecosystem. You won’t just be part of our FTI team, but you will also have a role on the teams of our clients. You will be part of a group whose projects have included, among many others: Advising a fortune 100 technology company on metaverse design and governance Serving the Unsecured Creditors Committee in the Voyager bankruptcy proceedings Performing M&A due diligence assessments and validation of assets under custody for many of the largest acquisitions in the industry Developing, designing, and building blockchain solutions for companies looking to improve supply chain and ESG tracking. Performing investigations on more than 75 cryptocurrency disputes. Basic Qualifications What You Will Need To Succeed You have deep functional expertise in one or more of the following: Blockchain technology (supply chain and ESG experience a plus) Cryptocurrencies and their supporting technologies (wallets, custody, tracing technology, etc.) NFT’s Metaverse You bring 6+ years of relevant full-time work experience, ideally working within consulting and/or Fortune 500 companies with a minimum of two years in blockchain and digital assets. You have proven ability to manage client engagements, client relationships, and provide thought-leadership to teams, owning the responsibility for the quality of engagements. A combination of management and hands-on delivery experience is critical. You possess the ability to support business development activities with emerging technology in a highly dynamic environment, understand business challenges, explain our offerings and services to provide value and identify opportunities for differentiated offerings based on blockchain and/or digital assets. Your story-telling ability enables you to explain blockchain outcomes and results in the context of the business and/or industry to make it actionable. Your ability to identify clients’ high-level business needs leads the creation of detailed use cases and functional specs. Testimony experience is a significant plus. Bachelor’s degree Preferred Skills You possess outstanding written and speaking skills; must be able to create status reports, write official reports, forensic reports, and demonstrate an ability to convey the complexity of blockchain and digital assets in easy-to-understand ways. You bring experience with building high-performing teams in an accelerated growth environment. Your well-developed analytical skills give you the ability to provide clarity to complex issues and synthesize large amounts of information. You have experience in building high-performing teams in an accelerated growth environment. FTI Consulting is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, protected veteran status, religion, physical or mental disability, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, or any other basis protected by law, ordinance, or regulation. Compensation Minimum Pay: $140,500 Maximum Pay: $185,000 Compensation Disclosure: The compensation range reflects potential base salary for the role. Actual compensation is determined based on a wide array of relevant factors including market considerations, business needs, and an individual’s location, skills, level of experience, and qualifications.

The Field Lead Representative is also responsible for performing daily, weekly, quarterly, and annual inspections on various tools, equipment, and other facility items, in compliance with company policies and regulatory standards. linkedin_detail_4452492430.description: Department: LNG Operations Location: US LA Cameron - LNG Facility Description About Us: The Caturus platform founded by Kimmeridge – an alternative asset manager focused on the energy sector – supports Kimmeridge’s overarching goal of providing low-cost energy on demand with the lowest carbon footprint. Kimmeridge’s vision in creating Caturus is to build the only independent, fully integrated natural gas and LNG export platform in the U.S. through a combination of its upstream operations and via Commonwealth LNG, a 9.5 million tonnes per annum liquefied natural gas export terminal in southwestern Louisiana on the U.S. Gulf Coast. The combined entities are committed to delivering responsibly sourced, low-emission fuel to domestic and international markets. Caturus is a Houston-based, private exploration and production company seeking to materially grow production through development of deep, high pressure, dry gas windows of the Eagle Ford and Austin Chalk, as well as Haynesville formations located in Texas and Louisiana while maintaining a relentless focus on safety. Commonwealth LNG was founded by industry veterans who decided to re-engineer the LNG construction model. Using proven best practices, Commonwealth is committed to building a world-class LNG export facility while focusing on safety, managing risk and achieving best-in-class environmental standards. Job Description Position Summary: The HSSE Coordinator ensures safe, compliant operations in Liquefied Natural Gas by implementing policies, conducting training, managing risk, investigating incidents, and overseeing compliance with maritime/terminal regulations for LNG carriers and facilities, often involving emergency response coordination and documentation for global energy companies. This position requires the ability to work both day and night shift. Key Accountabilities: Develop, implement, and monitor HSE policies, ensuring adherence to regulations (like USCG 33CFR127) and industry standards (including OGP). Perform risk assessments, conduct site inspections, lead incident investigations, analyze data (KPIs), and manage corrective actions to support safe delivery work outcomes. Coach peers and workforce for safe work delivery Capability to promote a strong safety culture and inspire personnel to safe work practices. Maintain HSE records, logs, and reports, ensuring data accuracy for management and audits. Act as a liaison between EPCM and Owners team. Interface with EPCM subcontractors executing work. Performing daily job site walk-downs for conformance to working processes and procedures including PTW and JSAs Reviewing and analyzing HSE data (leading/lagging indicators) for predictive analysis Qualifications : Education, Certificates, and Licenses: Bachelor's degree preferred. Work and life experiences related to job will be considered. Experience: 10+ years as HSSE Coordinator or relevant working experience. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Strong understanding of HSE principles in energy sectors. Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership abilities. Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills.

linkedin_detail_4453070375.description: This role is IN PERSON at our office in Miami, Florida. Do not apply if you cannot accommodate this. Senior Blockchain Architect Company Description Global Settlement (globalsettlement.com) is an institutional-grade blockchain network designed to seamlessly bridge traditional banking and digital markets through stablecoins, commodities, FX, and RWAs. Imagine the global settlement power of SWIFT, but modernized for real-time, regulated digital asset transactions. Role Description We're hiring a Senior Blockchain Architect to join our existing team and work across our blockchain, settlement network, and every part of our technology stack. This is not a greenfield build. We already have a lot of technology in production, and we need someone who can come in, understand it deeply, and help architect and extend it. This is a full-time, hands-on engineering role on our blockchain infrastructure team. This is a hands-on coding role, not a purely advisory or oversight one. You'll architect our core chain, covering node infrastructure, consensus, cross-chain systems, and protocol-level design, and then write the production code that brings that architecture to life. We expect you to be in the codebase daily: shipping features, reviewing pull requests, and debugging production systems alongside the team. "Architect" here means you have the experience to make the system-level calls and the hands to implement them, not that you hand designs to someone else to build. What You'll Do Design and implement work across our blockchain node infrastructure and settlement protocol, owning both the architecture and the code that ships it Write, review, and merge production code daily in Rust, Go, and/or Solidity; set the bar for quality through the code you contribute, not just the standards you write Define and evolve consensus design (PoA, PoS, BFT variants) for enterprise-grade performance and finality, and build it Architect and implement cross-chain communication and bridging systems for multi-network interoperability Lead the RFC and design-review process, then turn those decisions into working systems; make and document the high-stakes build-vs-buy and protocol-selection calls Debug and harden production systems, including consensus edge cases, node performance, and on-chain security, hands-on Evaluate emerging protocols, L1/L2 architectures, and settlement patterns, and translate research into shipped code Establish the security, scalability, and reliability principles every chain-level system is held to, and enforce them in the codebase Mentor senior engineers through code and design review, raising the technical bar across the engineering organization Own architecture decision records, technical standards, and the reference implementations behind them What You Bring 8+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years in blockchain, and a track record of both owning system architecture and personally writing the production code behind it You are a hands-on engineer today, still shipping code, not someone who has moved fully into management or advisory work Strong, current coding ability in Rust and/or Go (Solidity a plus). We'll expect to see it in the interview and take-home Deep expertise in blockchain node infrastructure, consensus algorithms, and protocol-level design, demonstrated through systems you've architected and built Strong working knowledge of blockchain platforms such as Ethereum, Cosmos, Hyperledger, or comparable L1/L2 networks Solid command of cryptographic primitives, key management, and on-chain security practices Experience building for cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) A record of production blockchain infrastructure at scale, systems you both designed and wrote The ability to make decisive technical calls, defend them with clear reasoning, and bring teams along Nice to Have Experience architecting stablecoin systems, CBDC infrastructure, or RWA tokenization Familiarity with cross-chain protocols and interoperability standards Background in financial services, payments, or regulated settlement systems Understanding of regulatory and compliance requirements in digital asset markets Note: This is a hands-on, chain-level engineering role. The "Architect" title reflects the seniority and system-ownership we expect, not a step back from coding. The core focus is consensus, node operations, cross-chain systems, and protocol design, and you'll be building all of it. If you're looking for a purely advisory, oversight, or people-management position where you don't write code, this isn't it. Equally, if your experience is solely smart-contract development, or implementation without ownership of system-level design, it likely isn't the right fit either. Why Join Global Settlement Ground-floor opportunity to architect settlement infrastructure used by sovereign and enterprise clients Direct impact on how digital assets move through the global financial system Work at the intersection of blockchain infrastructure, traditional finance, and regulatory innovation Join us at Global Settlement and help build the future of digital payments through institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure.

linkedin_detail_4454353769.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second Tier Candidates Include All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope Addressing the Prevention of and Response to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH) is a priority within IOM and a strong contributor to United Nations (UN) and Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) efforts at both the global and country levels. IOM’s PSEAH strategy focuses on five key pillars: 1) Leadership and Organizational Culture; 2) Institutional Accountability and Transparency; 3) Capacity-Development, Training, and Communication; 4) Quality and Accessible Victim Assistance; 5) Partnership and Coordination. Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission and in close coordination with the Regional PSEAH Officer and the global PSEAH Unit at Headquarters (HQ) , as well as relevant thematic specialists within the Country Office, Regional Office, and HQ, the Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH) Officer will be responsible and accountable for overseeing and managing IOM’s PSEAH prevention and response efforts in IOM Iraq, providing in line with a victim-centred approach. They will also be an active member of the inter-agency PSEA Network or Task Force in-country. Responsibilities Coordination Provide expert support for the development of an operational PSEAH Work Plan, in line with IOM and United Nations (UN) strategic frameworks, and in coordination with the global PSEAH Unit, Regional PSEAH Officer, and senior management in IOM Iraq. Ensure the inclusion of PSEAH within the IOM Iraq’s Country Strategy, Crisis Response Plans/Migrant Response Plans or other appeals as appropriate; ensure SEAH risks are considered in the risk register of the mission and that PSEAH is mainstreamed in project proposal development, programming, monitoring and evaluation and budgeting; develop PSEAH programming and liaise with relevant donors. Actively participate and engage to the in-country interagency PSEA Network activities (contribute to the development of the collective PSEA workplan, risk management plans, PSEA strategies, Standard Operating Procedures for an inter-agency Community-Based Complaint Mechanism, etc), and actively participate in IOM internal coordination initiatives. Coordinate the collection, analysis and use of data relation to PSEAH efforts, in line with relevant IOM data protection standards, to showcase trends, results and impact. Showcase PSEAH results and good practices through internal and external reporting, visibility materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives, in coordination with global and regional PSEAH teams. Prevention Undertake assessments to identify potential SEAH risks and define appropriate mitigation measures; in coordination with relevant units, ensure that mitigation measures are integrated into IOM programming, operations and administration. Develop a PSEAH training plan for the Country Office, organize and deliver trainings for IOM personnel, implementing partners , and key institutional stakeholders; support PSEAH focal points in delivering key messaging and trainings at country level, as appropriate. On a regular basis, compile and report data on the number of IOM personnel and partners trained in country on PSEAH in coordination with HR. Oversee the accurate registration of all participants in the IOM system and ensure timely issuance of certificates. Develop, localize and contextualize, and implement communication and awareness-raising strategies and tools to ensure appropriate PSEAH messaging and understanding of prohibited behaviours, reporting channels, available assistance. Map existing community engagement projects in country and work with project/programme managers to gather community input, insert PSEAH messages, and strengthen and/or establish safe and accessible reporting channels. Response Provide inputs to the development and mapping of country-specific interagency

linkedin_detail_4449099989.description: This is primarily an offshore position Company Overview Morrison, an energy service company, delivers infrastructure projects to clients in the oil and gas and renewables industries. For four decades, customers continue to rely on our specialized services and practical approach toward project execution. Position Overview The function of the position is to ensure that workplaces operate safely, comply with regulations, and minimize environmental impact. This position also serves as the central point of contact for HSE processes and asset administration serving as an impartial onsite resource, helping to strengthen a positive safety culture across the asset. Key Job Responsibilities Work in conjunction with the Vessel Superintendent, Captain and Dive Supervisor to promote and advance the safety culture on each assigned asset. Compile reports, make recommendations, and communicate observations or concerns to vessel leadership. Collect, track and trend the observation cards written by the crew members and provide the Vessel Leadership with a ZAPP Card trending chart to be addressed in the pre-shift safety meetings. Prepare the agenda, document the minutes, and facilitate HSE Site Committee meetings. Develop and coordinate hazard hunt schedules, assign personnel, identify target areas, and document, track and report findings. Submit Job Safety Analysis (JSA) to Management for desktop audits; provide feedback and coach crew members to improve JSA process. Provide feedback to the crew, coach and mentor crew members to enhance the JSA process on the asset. Assist the vessel leadership in preparing and submitting reports based on findings of incidents that may occur. Share lessons learned with crew members. Facilitate HSE training to crew members as needed or directed by management. Tally the weekly total of all leading and trailing indicators into the CMC HPIR report. Have the vessel leadership review the report and submit to the intended recipients. Perform Administrative/Clerical functions including Daily Field Reports (DFR), time sheets, dive logs, Personnel on Board (POB), customer request, answer phones, VHF Radio and requisitions. Job Skills & Education Highschool diploma or equivalent Minimum 3 years' experience in safety coordination in offshore, construction, or oil & gas. Familiarity with offshore systems, subsea technology, and asset integrity management. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement Morrison Energy is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. Morrison Energy is a drug-free workplace. The above description is intended to capture the essential functions of the job, nature and level of work as of the preparation date. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties that may be required of the position. This job description may be modified at any time with or without notice.

linkedin_detail_4454539367.description: Who we are About Bridge We're creating an entirely new payments platform, built with stablecoins, to simplify global money movement. Bridge enables faster, cheaper payments and borderless access to dollars via stablecoins. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders faster and cheaper vs. SWIFT and other fiat-only rails. Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We believe many trillions of dollars will move and settle through stablecoin payment rails. Bridge is pulling this future forward. We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that allows for the improvement of global money movement. About The Role As one of the first blockchain engineers at Bridge, you'll have the autonomy to work on projects that are truly global in scale and aim to give customers access to products they've never had access to. Many of the use cases that we work on today didn't exist several months ago, and that's because our team is dedicated to constant improvement for our partners and end users. Our engineers have outsized ownership over projects, so if you're looking for increased autonomy working on a completely greenfield opportunity, Bridge is the place for you. Responsibilities Build out multi-chain hot wallet infrastructure to support increased reliability of our payments. Build smart contracts to increase hot wallet payment throughput. Build smart contract platform to issue custom stablecoins across multiple blockchains (EVM, Solana, Stellar, etc.). Build smart contract monitoring systems to detect anomalous events (especially related to minting and burning). Design and develop blockchain-based applications and protocols to support stablecoin transactions and integrations. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand business requirements and translate them into technical specifications. Implement and maintain smart contracts, ensuring security and efficiency. Perform thorough testing and debugging of blockchain applications. Optimize blockchain performance and scalability. Stay up-to-date with the latest developments in blockchain technology and integrate relevant advancements into our solutions. Provide technical guidance and support to other team members. Contribute to the overall architecture and design of our blockchain systems. Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field We're open to hiring engineers at various levels of seniority, but in general we'd look for somebody with 5+ years of experience Strong proficiency in blockchain platforms such as Ethereum, Solana, or others Experience with smart contract development using Solidity or other relevant languages Deep understanding of cryptographic principles and blockchain protocols Experience with decentralized finance (DeFi) and stablecoins is highly desirable Knowledge of security best practices in blockchain development An enlarged sense of ownership and the ability to lead and influence the design and direction of our products An ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment A growth mindset, constant curiosity, and fearlessness to dive into the unknown Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clear technical documentation Preferred Qualifications Past experience working on crypto or financial products a plus, and while not required, we do look for people who are very passionate about building in this space Experience with building API products a plus, but not required Experience working with blockchain or distributed systems a big plus In-office expectations Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible. Pay and benefits The annual US base salary range for this role is $190,400 - $285,600. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process. Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends. We look forward to hearing from you. At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description.

linkedin_detail_4252632351.description: Call for Experts – Short-term Technical Assistance Technical Assistance Facility for Iraq (TAFFI 2.0) BACKGROUND Adam Smith International is a global advisory company that works locally to transform lives by making economies stronger, societies more stable, and governments more effective. The Technical Assistance Facility for Iraq 2.0 (TAFFI 2.0) is a 3-year programme that started in May 2024 and running until March 2027. In this new phase, TAFFI 2.0 will support anti-corruption efforts, serious and organised crime (SOC), improve cybersecurity capacities and support defence and security reform initiatives. ICED will support economic governance, Public Finance Management and civil service reform, and enhancing service delivery. Both programmes will scope the needs and offer support to selected government institutions, advising them on their strategies, policies, processes and adherence to international standards. The support is designed to be strategic, catalytic and sustainable and can often involve coordination with other donors and implementing partners. Cybersecurity: Experience in identifying, preventing, and mitigating cyber threats, including knowledge of advanced persistent threats, malware, ransomware, and network intrusions. Economic Governance: Experience working with governance and public administration authorities to support reforms to Public Financial Management, Civil Service, and Service Delivery. , Job Requirements We will give special consideration to applications that, on top of relevant experience on the above technical areas, can demonstrate some or all following assets: Experience working in Iraq and/or knowledge of the current political context in Iraq. Experience working with senior levels of government to provide advice and expertise on the reform of policies, procedures and structures. Experience designing and providing training, mentoring and/or expert capacity-building to senior government officials. Relevant experience within the British Government in at least one of the technical areas mentioned above. Experience working on an FCDO-funded project overseas and/or on a technical assistance facility/fund. A deep understanding of UK policy priorities on the technical areas mentioned and knowledge of relevant international networks, best practices and policies to which TAFFI could contribute. Cross-cutting expertise or knowledge of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) and Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) within an FCDO programme. linkedin_detail_4444080332.description: About The Role As a Senior Blockchain Engineer at Ondo, you will own the design of our smart contract systems - not just the contracts themselves, but how they're deployed, secured, monitored, and managed across their entire lifetime, and how they connect to the people and products that depend on them. You'll think about how a smart contract design decision ripples outward, to the web app, to the teams operating the system day to day, and ultimately to our end users. You'll collaborate with product, legal, compliance, web, and ops to make sure contracts are technically sound, regulatorily aligned, and genuinely operable by the teams who rely on them day to day. Tooling & Automation: Build tooling and automated systems that let non-technical teammates safely view, monitor, and manage contracts without writing scripts or touching raw chain operations directly. Cross-Functional Integration: Connect smart contract design to the rest of the product — helping the web team integrate cleanly, helping operational teams monitor and manage without direct scripting, and ensuring design decisions flow sensibly through to end users. Requirements Based in PT, MT, CT, or ET time zones. Excellent technical and non-technical communication skills, verbal and written. Strong competency with Solidity; exposure to non-EVM smart contract languages a plus — particularly Solana. linkedin_detail_4436853453.description: POSITION SUMMARY: Targa Resources is a leading provider of midstream services and is one of the largest independent midstream energy companies in North America, with assets in Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, North Dakota, and Louisiana. Targa owns, operates, acquires, and develops a diversified portfolio of complementary midstream energy assets. We encourage your interest in joining our team and pursuing the many opportunities we have at Targa. Targa has an immediate opportunity for a Safety Specialist located at the Watford City field office in Watford City, ND. The position supports the North Dakota Area business unit including the gas plants and the associated gathering systems and the crude and terminal system. This position will assist operations in achieving Targa’s goals with respect to compliance, industrial hygiene, and safety practices in our operations. A proven ability to solve problems, learn new material, adapt to change and be an effective communicator are key traits to success in this position. All the field ES&H positions in Targa receive support and guidance from the Corporate ES&H staff who provide subject matter expertise. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES: Site contact for all safety and health activities including emergency response and incident reporting. Participating and/or leading incident reporting and investigations, including Root Cause Analysis (RCA). Assist Process Safety Management Department (PSM) with implementation of PSM related activities. Managing and driving to completion open action items that result from PSM Audits, PHAs and other compliance Audits. Coordinate training of employees, including new hire orientations and monthly safety meetings, on ES&H requirements to ensure compliance with regulations and corporate safety programs and policies. Assist with internal and external compliance audits, as needed. Advise management, operations, and project/maintenance teams to assure compliance with federal, state, local and organizational rules and regulations pertaining to employee health and safety, acting as the local subject matter expert or resource. Implementation and auditing of OSHA programs and policies as well as local and state programs. Perform behavior-based safety observations. Assist with construction, contractors, shutdowns, confined space entries, critical lifts and other high priority jobs. Evaluate working conditions and recommend improvements in safety and health methods, practices, and procedures. Actively promote safe and environmentally friendly work processes within the facilities. Conduct Emergency Response drills and work with local emergency response agencies. Assure that various reports are filed with appropriate agencies in accordance with applicable safety regulations including specific requirements of permits or regulations for the various facilities. Assist other ES&H team members with company initiatives and overall implementation of ES&H Department Goals. Other duties as assigned. MINIMUM ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS: B.S. in Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Physics or Environmental Science or Safety. Intermediate level desktop computer skills using Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Physical ability to work at the plant site and accompany regulators on plant tours. Fluent English verbal and written skills. Must demonstrate strong communication skills. Ability to travel away from the area overnight periodically for training and company meetings. Ability and willingness to respond to calls after hours, if operational needs arise. Regular and reliable attendance. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: 3+ years of direct job experience. Direct experience in consulting or related industry. A collaborative personality, ready to work in teams and with others to solve problems. OSHA Certifications. Ability to interface effectively with all levels within the company as well as organizations outside the company (regulatory agencies, contractors, consultants). Effective project management skills. linkedin_detail_4454751928.description: Job Purpose The CCTV Operator is responsible for monitoring the hotel's CCTV surveillance systems to ensure the safety and security of guests, staff members, visitors, and hotel property. The CCTV Operator continuously monitors live and recorded footage, identifies and reports suspicious or unusual activities, and maintains accurate records of incidents. The role requires a high level of concentration, confidentiality, professionalism, and effective communication with the Security Department and other relevant departments. What You Will Do Responsibilities and essential job functions include but are not limited to the following: Follow Divan standards, policies, and SOPs at all times. Maintain personal hygiene and a professional appearance at all times. Be present on duty in a clean and immaculate uniform. Monitor all CCTV cameras and surveillance systems continuously and attentively. Ensure that CCTV cameras are functioning properly and report any technical issues or malfunctions immediately. Monitor hotel entrances, exits, public areas, back-of-house areas, parking areas, and other designated locations. Identify and report suspicious, unusual, or unauthorized activities to the Security Supervisor/Manager immediately. Monitor security incidents and provide accurate information to the Security team when required. Review recorded CCTV footage when requested for investigations or security-related incidents. Maintain confidentiality regarding CCTV footage, security incidents, and all information obtained through surveillance systems. Ensure that CCTV recordings and other surveillance information are handled securely and only accessed by authorized personnel. Maintain an accurate CCTV monitoring log, including incidents, observations, equipment issues, and other relevant information. Record and report all unusual incidents, accidents, thefts, unauthorized access, or suspicious behavior. Immediately inform the Security Supervisor/Manager of any noteworthy incident or condition. Assist the Security team during emergencies, including fire, theft, accidents, suspicious activities, bomb threats, and other security-related incidents. Monitor emergency situations through CCTV and provide relevant information to the Security team and management. Maintain a thorough knowledge of the hotel's layout, facilities, entrances, exits, restricted areas, and key security points. Maintain a complete understanding of emergency procedures and strictly follow established protocols. Communicate effectively with Security Officers, Security Supervisors, the Security Manager, and other departments when necessary. Contact the Security Manager/Supervisor in situations not covered by established instructions or whenever clarification is required. Ensure that all CCTV monitoring activities comply with hotel policies, security procedures, and applicable privacy and confidentiality requirements. Conduct proper handover at the end of each shift, including communicating ongoing incidents, observations, and equipment issues to the incoming operator. Maintain a professional, alert, and attentive approach throughout the entire shift. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with colleagues and other hotel departments. Perform any other duties related to security and surveillance as assigned by the Security Manager. Qualifications Minimum 2 years of experience as a CCTV Operator, Security Officer, or in a similar security surveillance role. Previous experience in a hotel or hospitality environment is preferred. Good knowledge of CCTV monitoring systems and surveillance equipment. Ability to identify suspicious behavior and respond appropriately to security incidents. Good command of English is required; knowledge of additional languages is considered an advantage. Basic computer skills and the ability to operate CCTV monitoring and recording systems. Strong observation and concentration skills. Excellent communication skills and a pleasant personality are required. Honest, trustworthy, reliable, and able to maintain strict confidentiality. Very energetic, flexible, and able to work effectively under pressure. Fully conversant with health, safety, security, and emergency procedures. Able to remain alert and focused for extended periods. Willing to work flexible shifts, including evenings, weekends, public holidays, and long hours when required.

linkedin_detail_4434003063.description: About The Company Tools for Humanity (TFH) designs and builds technology behind World. World is building a real human network designed to accelerate people in the age of AI. As bots and autonomous agents reshape the internet, people, institutions, and applications need a trusted way to confirm who is a real human while preserving privacy. The TFH and World tech stacks make this possible: the Orb verifies real, unique people, World ID proves it privately, and World App puts these capabilities, and more, in people’s hands. Together, they add a human layer to an AI-driven internet. World is already running at a global scale. More than 17 million people across 160 countries have verified with World ID, and more new Orb verifications take place each week. World App is already among the most used wallets globally. Developers are integrating World ID to build safer online experiences and create spaces where real people can participate, earn, and be recognized in ways AI simply can’t replicate. Founded in 2019, TFH has more than 400 people across hardware, software, AI, cryptography, mobile engineering, and global operations. Our teams come from OpenAI, Tesla, SpaceX, Apple, Google, Stripe, Meta, Coinbase, Palantir and MIT Media Lab. We’re backed by leading investors, including a16z, Khosla Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Blockchain Capital, Variant, Tiger Global, and Coinbase Ventures, as well as prominent operators and founders across fintech and AI. TFH and World have been featured on the cover of TIME Magazine, highlighted in Fast Company’s Next 5 in Fintech, and explored in a Bloomberg deep dive. Support business growth and project development through HSE reviews, risk assessments, and compliance evaluations. Strengthen stakeholder relationships and maintain effective engagement with regulators, tenants, contractors, and government authorities Qualifications Educational and Technical Qualifications: Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or related discipline. Lead Auditor certification in ISO 45001 and/or ISO 14001 is preferred. Additional certifications in COSHH, HSE Risk Management, Advanced First Aid, and Control of Major Accident Hazards are advantageous. Strong knowledge of Process Safety, Risk Assessment, Emergency Management, Environmental Compliance, and Integrated Management Systems. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications and report preparation. Language Skills: Excellent command of Arabic and English (written and spoken). Years of Experience: Minimum 7–10 years of progressive HSE experience within Oil & Gas, refinery, marine, industrial, or similar high-risk environments. Nature of Experience: Proven experience in Oil & Gas operations and associated HSE management systems. Experience in contractor management, regulatory compliance, emergency response, and operational risk management. Strong analytical skills with proven experience in incident investigation, trend analysis, and implementation of preventive measures. Experience working with multiple stakeholders, including regulators, tenants, contractors, and internal operational teams.

linkedin_detail_4458501641.description: This position is the company’s subject-matter expert for occupational safety compliance, incident investigation, and HS&E management systems. The position owns the integrity of the company’s HS&E data and reporting, leads investigation and root cause analysis of significant events, maintains company HS&E policies and procedures, and serves as the company’s primary point of contact with OSHA and with the Texas Railroad Commission and Texas Commission on Environmental Quality on safety-related matters. The position also supports environmental regulatory reporting in a coordinating role, owning the underlying event data, threshold screening, and tracking to closure in a manner that facilitates permitting and environmental submissions by the regulatory function. This is a senior individual-contributor role requiring strong, trusting relationships with Operations. The position holds unconditional stop-work authority and a defined escalation path, both described below. Essential Duties and Responsibilities This position comes with the following minimum set of responsibilities and requires an individual to be proficient in performing the listed duties. Maintain OSHA recordkeeping Forms 300, 300A, and 301, including recordability decisions, annual summary posting and certification, and electronic submission where required. Serve as the company’s point of contact for OSHA and for events requiring reporting to regulatory bodies in Texas. Support inspections and agency inquiries and track commitments to closure. Track regulatory changes affecting upstream operations and advise leadership on operational impact. Facilitate lower-severity investigations with an Operations leader in the chair, quality-review investigations closed by others, and train and qualify field supervisors as investigation leads. Own the corrective action process: track to closure, verify effectiveness rather than completion, and escalate overdue items. Issue field-usable lessons learned from every closed significant-event investigation and confirm they reach the crews. Own the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of HSE data in the incident management system, ISNetworld, and related systems — entry rules, controlled vocabularies, validation, user training, and audit. Trend high-potential and SIF-potential events and keep severity-potential classification accurate so exposure stays visible independently of outcome. Define, publish, and review the leading indicator set, and report performance and trends to leadership through Excel and Power BI. Screen releases against applicable reporting thresholds, document each determination, and route reportable events to the environmental and regulatory function. Maintain HSE policies and procedures, including revision control and verification that field locations hold current versions. Own the ISNetworld account and contractor qualification systems, including documentation, compliance monitoring, and client and contractor requests for information. Set HSE expectations with contractors before work begins and verify orientation and training requirements are met. Review contractor HSE performance beyond prequalification scores, include contractor events in company trending, and apply escalation criteria up to removal from company work. Maintain the HSE training curriculum, driven by investigation findings and data trends, and deliver or coordinate its delivery. Visit field locations on a defined cadence to observe work, engage crews and supervisors, and verify that HSE systems work in the field and not only on paper. Support driving and motor vehicle safety, including journey management, motor vehicle record review, and applicable DOT requirements. Support emergency response planning and drills and lead after-action reviews following significant events. All other duties and responsibilities assigned by management. Qualifications & Skills Below are the minimum education, experience, and skills required or preferred for this position. Education/Experience High school diploma or equivalent required. Bachelor's degree in occupational safety, environmental health, or a related field preferred. 10 years of experience in oil and gas or a similar industrial industry. Minimum of 5 years of experience in leading HS&E roles in the oil and gas field. Experience conducting incident investigations and root cause analysis. Other Skills Familiarity with OSHA recordkeeping and reporting requirements. Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive personal, incident, and investigation data. Computer Skills Full knowledge of MS Office, with an emphasis on Excel and Power BI. Working knowledge of ISNetworld or other contractor prequalification platforms. Certificates and Licenses Certification in a formal root cause analysis methodology like TapRooT or Kelvin Top-Set. OSHA 10 or 30-Hour General Industry or Construction certification a plus.

linkedin_detail_4459046105.description: Job Title Global Vice President, Environmental, Health & Safety Overview Fleet Data Centers designs, builds and operates mega-scale data center campuses. Fleet provides its customers with flexibility and predictability to meet their upside demand forecasts, addressing a key need in the market as traditional leased models are struggling to keep pace with the demand for new Cloud and AI infrastructure. Fleet is led by a team of industry veterans that have already made a lasting imprint on the evolution of global digital infrastructure and are committed and uniquely capable of upleveling data center development scale and operations in the face of rising demand. Fleet is well positioned to bring in-house design, engineering and operational capabilities to collaborate with customers on tailored solutions for campuses of 500MW+. This unique model enables Fleet to provide the world’s largest and most sophisticated customers with a seamless extension of their own data center fleets with constant access to design innovation. Fleet is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with satellite offices in Seattle, WA and Arlington, VA. Position Overview The Global Vice President, Environmental, Health & Safety is Fleet's most senior EHS leader, accountable for the entire EHS management system across every phase of the business, from design and construction through commissioning and live mission-critical operations. This role owns Fleet's EHS policy, standards, procedures, and assurance framework globally, while directing a field organization of Directors, Managers, and Specialists who execute at each campus. The Global VP EHS is accountable for three outcomes: zero preventable incidents, an audit-ready compliance posture across all jurisdictions, and an EHS management system mature enough to scale without dilution as Fleet adds campuses. Positioned within the DC EHS & Security organization, this leader partners daily with Physical Security, Design & Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Operations leadership, and is the executive voice of EHS to Fleet's president, customers, insurers, and General Contractor executives. Job Responsibilities Construction EHS Leadership & Field Oversight Own EHS performance standards for General Contractors and all subcontractors across every active construction site, setting the tone through visible and felt leadership consistent with Fleet's Visible and Felt Leadership Procedure. Direct the Director of EHS Construction and site-level Construction Managers and Specialists across South Valley, Peru Ridge, and Caldwell Valley, ensuring the Global Construction EHS Policy is applied consistently regardless of site, region, or General Contractor. (OTC: HWKE) Location: Miami Beach, FL (On-site) – with regular travel to New York and other cities as needed| Full-Time, Exempt About Hawkeye Digital Hawkeye Digital Inc. (HWKE) is a publicly traded private equity and merchant banking platform focused on crypto and digital assets. We pursue strategic opportunities to develop and support next‑generation technologies, investing in, financing, and advising companies across the space — from structuring and inking multimillion-dollar deals to guiding portfolio companies through capital raises and the public listing process. We are a lean, senior team at an early inflection point, and Directors will help shape the merchant banking practice itself. The Opportunity We are hiring experienced merchant bankers (VP/Director level) to help build Hawkeye's practice. You will set up how we source, evaluate, and execute deals, then run your own transactions from first conversation through closing. You will represent Hawkeye directly to founders, investors, and our banking partners, and as the practice grows, you will help hire, develop, and manage the team. What You'll Do Lead deal origination: build and own your proprietary pipeline of investment, financing, and advisory opportunities across digital assets. Structure and negotiate transactions end-to-end, from term sheets through closing (including novel structures: fund vehicles, foundation-related entities, tokenized instruments). Direct due diligence and help set the firm's crypto-native valuation standards: comps frameworks, market benchmarks, and deal pricing. Lead capital raises for Hawkeye and its clients — quarterbacking banking relationships and driving direct institutional and strategic investor outreach. Serve as a senior client-facing advisor to portfolio companies via capital strategy, roadshows, public listing preparation, partnerships, and revenue growth. Build the merchant banking function itself: processes, materials standards, and, as the practice scales, hiring and managing junior deal professionals. Serve as a visible representative of Hawkeye in the market: conferences, investor meetings, and industry relationships both domestically (predominantly in Miami and New York) and internationally. Who You Are 7+ years of investment banking and/or private equity experience — M&A, capital markets, or principal investing — with a meaningful portion at the VP or Director level, and demonstrable fintech deal experience. You have structured, negotiated, and closed transactions across fintech, including payments, exchanges and trading platforms, asset and wealth management technology, banking infrastructure, and digital assets. Familiarity with the crypto and digital asset market is strongly preferred: comps, key players, founders, investors, and the network that comes with it. You have led deals, not just supported them, and you are comfortable being the most experienced transaction professional in the room. You have raised capital directly: sourced investors, run processes, and closed. Public-markets fluency is required: hands-on experience with IPOs, uplistings, PIPEs, reverse mergers, or operating inside a publicly traded platform. You are entrepreneurial and self-directed, comfortable operating with minimal infrastructure and building from a blank page. Based in Miami or committed to relocating; comfortable with regular travel to New York. This isn't about deploying speculative tokens; it’s about constructing highly resilient, mathematical, and adversarial-resistant software that remains upgradeable, cost-efficient, and bulletproof over time. The Role As a core protocol contributor, you will take deep ownership of smart contract architecture from initial mathematical modeling and design through to mainnet deployment, external audit facilitation, and live monitoring. • Protocol Architecture (40%): Design and implement secure, gas-optimized Solidity smart contracts for lending, borrowing, vaults, yield routing, liquidations, and access control. • Testing & Simulation (30%): Write extensive unit, integration, fork, fuzz, and invariant tests utilizing modern frameworks to ensure zero-day resiliency. • Security & Audits (15%): Prepare codebases for top-tier external audits, remediate findings, and design proactive on-chain risk mitigation/monitoring strategies. • Cross-Functional Integration (15%): Collaborate closely with risk, frontend, indexer, and quantitative engineering teams to build seamless, secure end-to-end dApps. The Must-Haves • Experience: 4+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 2+ years writing, deploying, and maintaining highly secure Solidity smart contracts in production.. • Tooling & Frameworks: Expert-level mastery of Foundry (Forge, Cast) including advanced fuzzing, invariant testing, and mainnet fork simulations. • EVM Deep Dive: Thorough understanding of EVM internals, storage layouts, gas optimization strategies, assembly (Yul), and standard proxy/upgradeability patterns. • DeFi Primitives: Practical, working knowledge of core financial primitives (such as ERC-20/4626/721/1155, AMMs, lending pools, oracles, and liquidation engines). • AI-Assisted Acceleration: Comfort using modern AI coding tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude, Copilot) to accelerate unit testing, documentation, and boilerplate development, backed by the critical judgment required never to trust raw model outputs blindly. • Security Mindset: An obsessive awareness of common attack vectors (reentrancy, oracle manipulation, front-running, rounding errors, and access-control flaws). The Bonus Skills • Audit Pedigree: Prior experience guiding a protocol through a major external audit (e.g., Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin, Spearbit) or participating in competitive security audits. • Multi-Chain/SVM: Exposure to Rust-based smart contract environments (SVM/Solana, CosmWasm) or zero-knowledge (ZK) rollup architectures. • Advanced Automation: Familiarity with off-chain automation infrastructure like Keepers, Defender, or Gelato. Personal Traits • Adversarial Thinker: You don't just think about how code should work; you instinctively try to find ways to break, front-run, or exploit the state machine you are building.. • Execution & Ownership: You act as an owner, not a ticket executor. You proactively trace edge cases, optimize gas, and address technical debt before it is flagged.. • Detail-Obsessed: You care about the nuance of a single uint256 math operation and understand why rounding down vs. up is a security-critical decision.. • Collaborative & Clear: You can distill complex cryptographic or financial system logic into clear documentation and explain architectural tradeoffs to non-smart contract engineers.. Location: Remote (with meaningful overlap with US/EU working hours)
