linkedin_detail_4460931486.description: About Polygon Labs Polygon Labs is a global blockchain payments company building and operating infrastructure to move money instantly, reliably, and at internet scale, with the mission to move all money onchain. It is building the Polygon Open Money Stack, an open and integrated stack of services and technologies to instantly and reliably move money anywhere, and put it to work. Its infrastructure has facilitated trillions of dollars in onchain value transfer and supported millions of transactions daily for some of the globe's largest banks, fintechs, enterprises, and consumer applications. Your Role Polygon has one product in the market: the Open Money Stack. It moves money across borders in seconds instead of days, through a single API instead of a stack of vendor contracts. Money movement only works if there is money on both ends of the corridor. That is the part most people underestimate. Someone has to line up the banks, the market makers, the custodians and the aggregators, then make the economics work corridor by corridor. Right now Polygon sources that liquidity deal by deal. It needs to become a function. That is this job. You own the partner side of the Open Money Stack and you build the liquidity leg underneath it. The pillar was created a few months ago and is still being shaped. You are not inheriting a finished machine. You are building one, with the mandate and the air cover to do it. Your Responsibilities Own the partner book. Banks, market makers and OTC desks, custodians, payout aggregators, ramp providers, compliance and licensing partners. You source them, negotiate them, sign them and keep them productive after signature. Build corridor liquidity. Work out what it costs to hold and move value in each priority corridor, across the Americas, Europe, Southeast Asia, Africa and the Gulf. Decide where to pre-fund, where to source on demand, and where a market maker partnership beats holding inventory. Model it properly. Defend the numbers. Make the unit economics real. Spreads, FX, settlement timing, trapped capital, fee structures. You will be the person in the room who knows whether a corridor makes money at volume, and who says so when it does not. Sit between Sales and the balance sheet. The sales team will sell corridors and volumes. You make sure the liquidity behind them exists at a price that works. When a large customer lands, you are part of the answer to "can we actually support this." Negotiate real agreements. Term sheets, MoUs, commercial contracts, revenue shares. Often with counterparties who are regulated, slow and careful, in markets where the rules changed last quarter. Build the team. The pillar grows as the business does. You will be hiring and shaping who does what. What You'll Need Real experience sourcing and managing liquidity, from a payments company, a market maker, an OTC desk, a bank treasury function or a crypto trading business. You have done this, not just watched it happen. Commercial negotiation with regulated institutions. Banks, PSPs, licensed exchanges. You know why these deals take nine months and how to make them take four. Fluency in stablecoin and FX mechanics. Where spread comes from, what settlement risk actually looks like, why pre-funding kills margin. Comfort with a model in Excel. Not a treasury quant, but you can build the case and stand behind the assumptions. Judgment about which partnerships are worth the effort. Most are not. Preferred Qualifications Depth in one or more live payment corridors, whichever region that happens to be. Existing relationships with market makers, custody providers or payout networks. Background spanning both traditional payments and crypto. Rare, and valuable here. What we are not looking for: someone who wants a defined process to run. This pillar does not have one yet. Perks Benefits The goal of the Polygon Labs total rewards program is to support the health and well-being of you and your family. Our comprehensive compensation plan includes the following benefits for our full time employees: Remote first global workforce Industry leading Medical, Dental and Vision health insurance* Company matching 401k with 3% match* $1,500 Home Office Set Up Allowance (life-time max) $200 Annual Book Allowance Program $75 Monthly internet or phone reimbursement Flexible Time Off Company issued laptop Egg freezing, mental health, and employee wellness benefits In certain countries medical, dental and vision is fully covered for employees & their dependents. This is country and plan specific. 401k is for United States employees only Polygon Labs is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Polygon Labs is committed to treating all people in a way that allows them to maintain their dignity and independence. We believe in integration and equal opportunity. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process and applicants with a disability may request to be accommodated throughout the recruitment process. We will work with all applicants to accommodate their individual accessibility needs. If you think you have what it takes, but don't necessarily meet every single point on the job description, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit. familiarity with Effect (effect.ts) or a comparable functional effect system is a plus Working familiarity with EVM transaction mechanics: ABI encoding, nonce management, gas estimation, revert handling, and event decoding Some production experience with Solidity smart contract development, including exposure to upgradeable proxy patterns (UUPS) and OpenZeppelin contract libraries Exposure to institutional custody or key management APIs is a strong plus, though not required Understanding of idempotency, at-least-once delivery, and crash recovery concepts in async systems Comfortable asking for help extending existing patterns while building toward independent ownership of larger features Nice to Haves Experience with ZKsync or ZK Stack-based chains—particularly developer-facing constraints like calldata handling, system contract interactions, and AA transaction formats Familiarity with Kafka or message-queue-backed async pipelines Prior work in fintech, payments, or any regulated financial infrastructure environment Foundry proficiency (forge test, forge fmt) What We Offer Competitive compensation Remote-first work environment Opportunity to shape a market-defining protocol with an experienced founding team Meaningful influence over product design at the earliest stage Interested in this role? About The Role You'll work within the systems that take a payment instruction and turn it into an immutable, on-chain record—implementing features and extensions within an established transaction pipeline architecture, alongside senior engineers who own its design. That means building out pieces of the integration layer between our backend services and our institutional custody platform, and contributing to transaction integrity from calldata construction through on-chain finality on our private ZKsync-based L2. You'll also work directly in our smart contract suite, extending existing contracts under established upgrade-safety and role-governance patterns, and building the audit trail and compliance evidence that regulated bank partners require. What You'll Do Implement components of the transaction lifecycle: calldata construction, custody platform signing requests, nonce handling, L2 submission, and finality confirmation, working within the pipeline architecture senior engineers on the team have designed Build features within the signing pipeline—new submission paths, throughput handling against custody platform rate limits, async transaction submission logic—under existing architectural patterns Implement payment integrity controls: commitment hash verification at pipeline handoff points and co-signer policy evaluation logic Extend our Solidity smart contracts, following established upgrade-safety, storage-layout, and role-governance conventions Contribute to the custody platform authorization policy integration and co-signer agent for custodian-owned transaction authorization Build structured audit trail logging from transaction origination through on-chain execution, satisfying evidentiary requirements for bank partners under regulatory oversight Contribute to the async transaction queue supporting tiered SLAs and per-bank throughput quotas Write high-coverage tests across backend services and smart contracts, maintaining our coverage threshold Participate in on-call, working through known issue patterns independently and escalating novel failure modes to senior engineers Qualifications 3–5 years of backend software engineering experience, with 1–2 years working directly on EVM-compatible blockchain systems Solid proficiency in TypeScript; familiarity with Effect (effect.ts) or a comparable functional effect system is a plus Working familiarity with EVM transaction mechanics: ABI encoding, nonce management, gas estimation, revert handling, and event decoding Some production experience with Solidity smart contract development, including exposure to upgradeable proxy patterns (UUPS) and OpenZeppelin contract libraries Exposure to institutional custody or key management APIs is a strong plus, though not required Understanding of idempotency, at-least-once delivery, and crash recovery concepts in async systems Comfortable asking for help extending existing patterns while building toward independent ownership of larger features Nice to Haves Experience with ZKsync or ZK Stack-based chains—particularly developer-facing constraints like calldata handling, system contract interactions, and AA transaction formats Familiarity with Kafka or message-queue-backed async pipelines Prior work in fintech, payments, or any regulated financial infrastructure environment Foundry proficiency (forge test, forge fmt) What We Offer Competitive compensation Remote-first work environment Opportunity to shape a market-defining protocol with an experienced founding team Meaningful influence over product design at the earliest stage Interested in this role? Send us your resume. ‹ Senior Data Engineer Senior Blockchain Engineer ›

linkedin_detail_4460703653.description: We are seeking an experienced Health & Safety professional, at Senior Officer or Manager level, to lead occupational health and safety at our terminal operations in Basra, Iraq. This is a hands-on, field-based role for someone comfortable operating in a challenging and complex operating environment, while maintaining close and structured coordination with head office and international financial institutions including the IFC. This role sits within a terminal operation financed in line with international standards, and the successful candidate will be expected to embed IFC Performance Standards (particularly PS2 on Labor and Working Conditions) into day-to-day site practice. Key Responsibilities Lead and manage the terminal's Health & Safety program, ensuring safe execution of all stevedoring activities, cargo handling, lifting, other terminal activities and full compliance with local Iraqi regulations, international maritime/port safety standards, and IFC Performance Standards. Maintain and continuously improve site-level H&S management systems (risk assessments, incident investigation, permit-to-work, emergency response planning, contractor management). Conduct regular field inspections and audits across terminal operations and contractors, identifying hazards and driving corrective action to closure. Build and maintain a strong safety culture among terminal staff, contractors, and third-party operators on site. Prepare clear, high-quality written reports (in English) for head office, shareholders, and IFC/lender reporting requirements — including incident reports, monthly H&S performance data, and periodic compliance updates. Liaise directly with IFC and/or other lenders during site visits, audits, or supervision missions, representing the terminal's H&S performance and improvement plans. Support implementation and continual improvement of the Occupational Health and Safety management system (ISO 45001) and the company health and safety procedures. Support emergency preparedness and response planning specific to the operating context in Basra. Manage relationships with local authorities, regulators, and emergency services as required. Mentor and build capability within the local H&S team over time. Candidate Profile Required: Significant professional experience (with a minimum of 6 years) in occupational health & safety management, ideally within ports, terminals, logistics, heavy industry, oil & gas, or infrastructure sectors. Working knowledge of IFC Performance Standards (particularly PS1 and PS2) and/or Equator Principles-aligned environments. Demonstrated ability to work independently in a demanding field environment while maintaining rigorous reporting discipline back to head office. Excellent written and spoken English — reporting quality and clarity are essential given the audience (shareholders, IFC, lenders). Willingness and ability to relocate to and reside in Umm Qasr, Iraq for a minimum of 2 years. Strong stakeholder management skills, with the composure to engage confidently with senior head office management and external financial institutions. Advantageous: Arabic language skills (spoken). Prior experience working in Iraq or comparable higher-risk/complex operating environments (Middle East, Africa, conflict-affected or post-conflict settings). Recognized H&S qualification (e.g., NEBOSH, IOSH, or equivalent). Experience supporting IFC/DFI site supervision missions or audits.

Strong experience managing construction projects, CAPEX budgets, cost estimation, budget tracking, and cost control. Working knowledge of MEP, cold-chain equipment specifications, and local building requirements. Good understanding of food storage requirements and grocery store setup. Proven experience managing store setup and fit-out projects. Strong knowledge of construction quality and safety standards. Experience managing store equipment, technical specifications, operational requirements, maintenance contracts, and shelving. Experience with grocery storage conditions and requirements. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to manage multiple sites, projects, and priorities in a fast-paced environment. Proficiency in project management tools. AutoCAD knowledge is preferred. Preferred Qualifications Experience in grocery, FMCG, quick-commerce, or dark-store expansion. Existing knowledge of the Iraqi commercial real estate and construction market. Experience working with landlords, contractors, equipment suppliers, and government authorities. Experience managing end-to-end store development projects. Experience with cold-chain equipment and grocery storage environments. Success Metrics Sites signed vs. plan Fit-out on-time completion rate Cost per store vs. CAPEX budget

linkedin_detail_4464021754.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Project Context and Scope Access to finance remains one of the principal barriers to business growth and job creation in Iraq. While significant efforts have been undertaken by the Government of Iraq and the Central Bank of Iraq to increase access to financing for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), many entrepreneurs continue to face challenges related to collateral requirements, perceived credit risks, limited financial histories, high transaction costs, and restricted access to suitable financial products. IOM Iraq supports livelihoods, economic recovery, and private sector development interventions aimed at fostering sustainable economic opportunities for vulnerable populations, including women, youth, returnees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), climate-affected communities, and small business owners. As part of its efforts to promote financial inclusion and strengthen sustainable economic recovery, IOM intends to establish a blended finance mechanism that utilizes catalytic donor funding alongside commercial lending to enhance access to finance for underserved businesses and entrepreneurs. The blended finance approach will seek to mobilize capital, reduce lending risks, strengthen financial institutions’ engagement with target populations, and promote sustainable market development. The initiative will be developed in close coordination with the Central Bank of Iraq, partner banks, and other financial institutions to ensure alignment with national priorities, banking regulations, and sustainable financial sector development objectives. To support this process, IOM seeks to recruit a qualified Blended Finance Specialist Consultant with substantial experience in banking, SME finance, financial inclusion, blended finance, and stakeholder engagement within the development and financial sectors. The consultant will work closely with IOM livelihoods teams, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), participating financial institutions, and other relevant stakeholders. The consultant will serve in an individual capacity and shall not be considered an IOM staff member. The consultancy contract does not establish an employer-employee relationship. The consultant shall have no authority to make commitments, representations, or decisions that bind IOM. Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing The consultant will be operating within the Peace and Recovery unit, Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Senior Programme Coordinator, in close coordination with the National Livelihood Officer The consultancy is open to international consultants and will be primarily based in Baghdad. However, field missions to the Kurdistan Region of Iraq will be required as part of the assignment. Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract Lead the design, development, and operationalization of the blended finance facility, providing strategic and technical guidance throughout implementation. Support the financial structuring process through financial modelling, analysis of financial, fiduciary, and operational risks associated with proposed financing arrangements, and review of concessional finance structures proposed by fund managers or financing partners, ensuring alignment with IOM's objectives, policies, and risk management requirements. Provide technical support to IOM in its engagement with the Central Bank of Iraq, partner banks, and other stakeholders, and support the development of cooperation, governance, and accountability frameworks. Establish the facility’s operational model, risk management framework, implementation procedures, and governance arrangements to ensure effective and sustainable delivery. Design and deliver capacity-building initiatives for IOM and partner stakeholders while establishing monitoring, evaluation, learning, and reporting systems to measure performance and impact. Develop a strategy for future partnerships, resource mobilization, and expansion of the facility, including a scale-up concept note and an engagement strategy for potential investors and donors. Objectives of the Assignment The overall objective of the consultancy is to support IOM Iraq in the assessment, design, development, and operationalization of an innovative blended finance facility, including providing technical advice during negotiations with financial institutions and development partners, following IOM’s Innovative Finance engagement models, capable of mobilizing concessional finance for underserved MSMEs and vulnerable entrepreneurs through strategic partnerships with the Central Bank of Iraq and participating financial institutions. linkedin_detail_4467227757.description: Company Description Blocknetics is a boutique consulting firm focused on helping organizations unlock the value of blockchain technology through end-to-end solutions. The company delivers tailored services across technology consulting, strategy development, staffing, and research and development (R&D), supporting clients at every stage of blockchain adoption. Blocknetics specializes in blockchain architecture and smart contract development, ensuring solutions are robust, scalable, and secure for private, public, and hybrid networks. The firm also offers strategic advisory to align blockchain initiatives with business goals and provides access to highly skilled blockchain professionals to support long-term success. Its R&D efforts keep clients ahead in a rapidly evolving blockchain landscape. Role Description The Senior Smart Contract Engineer is a full-time, hybrid role based in Atlanta, GA, with flexibility for partial work from home. This role is responsible for designing, implementing, and auditing smart contracts for a variety of client projects, ensuring security, reliability, and performance across different blockchain platforms. Day-to-day tasks include collaborating with consultants and client stakeholders to translate business requirements into technical specifications, writing clean and maintainable smart contract code, and integrating contracts with front-end and back-end systems. The engineer will review code, perform security assessments, contribute to architectural decisions, and help establish best practices for blockchain development within the firm. The role also involves mentoring junior engineers, participating in technical research, and supporting proposal development and technical documentation for client engagements. Qualifications Strong proficiency in smart contract languages and platforms (e.g., Solidity on Ethereum, Rust or Move on other chains), with experience in contract design, deployment, and interaction. Hands-on experience with blockchain development tools and frameworks (e.g., Hardhat, Truffle, Foundry, web3.js/ethers.js, node-based tooling) and version control (Git). Deep understanding of blockchain fundamentals, including consensus mechanisms, gas optimization, token standards (e.g., ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155), and on-chain/off-chain integration. Demonstrated expertise in security practices for smart contracts, such as threat modeling, common vulnerability patterns (e.g., re-entrancy, overflow, access control flaws), and familiarity with audit methodologies. Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into technical specifications, with strong documentation and communication skills. Background in software engineering with solid knowledge of data structures, algorithms, and testing practices (unit, integration, and automated testing for smart contracts). Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. linkedin_detail_4466272637.description: Our client is an established crypto infrastructure business expanding into trading. They are building a funded trading platform for crypto perpetuals, beginning with paper trading and moving toward evaluations, funded accounts and payouts. They are hiring a hands on leader to build and operate the trading risk engine behind that product. You will own the rules, exposure, hedging and payout economics that determine whether the platform can grow safely and profitably. This is not a compliance, audit or advisory position. You will make live risk and trading decisions, work directly with data and help build the underlying systems with Product and Engineering. The team intends to be aggressive on product. They are not looking for someone whose first response to risk is to block a feature, ban a trading style or tighten every limit. They want someone who can identify the real risk, quantify it and find a practical way to support the product through better pricing, smarter limits, targeted monitoring, trader segmentation, routing, hedging or staged rollouts. Restrictions should be precise and evidence based. Broad bans should be reserved for risks that cannot be measured or controlled. What You Will Own The firm's trading book, aggregate exposure and risk appetite Funded account rules, including drawdown, leverage, concentration and consistency parameters Reliable payout reviews, payout liability forecasting and reserve requirements Trader classification, including profitable, toxic, fraudulent and correlated behaviour Decisions about which activity remains simulated, is internalised, is matched internally or is hedged externally External hedging strategy and relationships with venues, liquidity providers and market makers Net exposure by instrument, strategy, trader cohort and correlated account group Margin, liquidation, circuit breaker and kill switch controls Real time monitoring, alerts, incident response and daily risk reporting Risk requirements for product, data and trading infrastructure Recruitment and leadership of the future risk and dealing team Trading and Execution Responsibilities Build the logic for A book, B book and hybrid routing across funded accounts Determine when the firm should hedge positions on external venues and when exposure can remain internal Measure shadow P&L so a trader's apparent profitability is tested against real fees, funding, spread, slippage and execution costs Configure and continuously review leverage, margin requirements, available instruments, spreads, mark ups and other trading conditions Monitor execution speed, fills, rejected orders, pricing anomalies, market gaps and platform incidents Investigate toxic flow, latency arbitrage, coordinated trading, copy trading, multi account abuse and attempts to exploit payout rules Lead the response during unusual volatility, system failures and concentrated exposure events Produce clear recommendations and risk reports for the founders and senior leadership Product and Commercial Partnership You will be the risk voice in product discussions from the beginning. Your role is to make informed risk taking possible, not to remove risk from the business. For every proposed feature, instrument, promotion or rule change, you should be able to explain: How trader behaviour may change and which risks matter How expected payouts and unit economics could be affected Which risks can be priced, limited, monitored, routed or hedged How to launch without weakening the product proposition Which evidence would justify expanding, changing or stopping the feature after launch The goal is not the lowest possible risk. It is to take the right risks deliberately, protect legitimate payouts and give the product room to win. What Success Looks Like Within your first six months, you will have: Established measurable risk limits and clear escalation procedures Built reliable exposure, payout and trader behaviour monitoring Implemented systematic trader segmentation and routing Created a fair and repeatable payout review process Built a clear framework for deciding when to simulate, internalise, match or hedge trades Validated hedging performance and external execution costs Enabled ambitious product launches with controls proportionate to the actual risk Created a scalable operating model for the risk and dealing function Ideal Background Five or more years in trading risk, dealing, quantitative trading, market making or a closely related function preferred Demonstrated ownership of live trading exposure is more important than tenure Direct experience with funded trader platforms, retail FX or CFD brokers, crypto derivatives exchanges, proprietary trading firms or market makers Strong knowledge of perpetuals, leverage, margin, liquidation, funding and market microstructure Practical experience with A book and B book management, hedging, routing and liquidity providers Experience analysing trader behaviour, trading abuse and correlated accounts Comfortable using SQL, Python or equivalent tools to work directly with trading data Able to translate risk logic into precise product and engineering requirements Strong commercial judgement across growth, trader experience, payouts and firm profitability Inventive and pragmatic, able to design controls that enable growth rather than defaulting to blanket restrictions Calm and decisive during volatile markets and operational incidents This Role Is Not Suitable If Your experience is primarily compliance, audit, credit policy or operational risk documentation You have advised trading teams but never owned live exposure or execution decisions You treat eliminating risk as the goal, or regularly default to saying no when a risk can be measured and managed You prefer creating frameworks over implementing and operating them You cannot work directly with data, engineers and imperfect early stage systems You are unwilling to make time sensitive decisions when the trading book is at risk

This role serves as the senior HS&E leader for a large, geographically dispersed operation encompassing company-owned retail sites, franchise locations, bakery operations, field teams, offices, and support functions across the United States. The Vice President is accountable for developing and delivering an integrated HS&E strategy that protects people, communities, assets, brand reputation, and business performance while enabling sustainable growth. The role ensures compliance with all regulatory requirements and bp standards while fostering a culture where safety, risk management, operational rigor, and environmental stewardship are embedded into every aspect of the business. Partnering closely with executive leadership, operations teams, franchise partners, and bp's central HS&E organization, the Vice President will establish enterprise-wide standards, strengthen risk management capabilities, drive continuous improvement, and ensure consistent execution of HS&E programs across a network supporting thousands of employees, contractors, customers, and business partners. This leader will provide oversight for operational risk management, process safety, occupational safety, environmental compliance, emergency preparedness and response, incident prevention, regulatory engagement, and business resilience. The role plays a critical part in enabling safe and reliable operations while supporting commercial performance, transformation initiatives, network growth, and long-term value creation. The Vice President will serve as a trusted advisor to bp’s US Convenience & Mobility leadership team, ensuring HS&E risks are identified, understood, and managed effectively while driving a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement throughout the organization. Key Accountabilities Own the USCM Health, Safety & Environmental strategy and operating plan, ensuring risks across sites, fueling operations and store environments are identified, managed and mitigated. Serve as the senior advisor to the USCM leadership on health, safety, environmental, security, and operational risk matters. Lead the USCM HSSE team, setting clear priorities, performance expectations and accountability for safety and environmental outcomes across the network. Maintain a strong dotted-line relationship with bp's central HSSE function to ensure USCM continues to apply enterprise standards, tools and governance expectations. Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state and local health, safety and environmental regulations, including DOT, OSHA and EPA requirements, across USCM's store and fueling network. Partner with Operations, Construction & Maintenance and Store Support teams to embed safety and environmental considerations into site design, store operations and field execution. Lead incident investigation, root cause analysis and corrective action processes, translating lessons learned into practical improvements at store level. Provide regular reporting on safety performance, environmental compliance and emerging risks to the USCM CEO and leadership team. Skills & Experience Significant experience in health, safety, environmental or risk management leadership, ideally within convenience retail, fuel retail, grocery or another multi-site operating environment. Strong understanding of HSSE regulatory requirements applicable to retail fueling and convenience store operations, including DOT, OSHA and EPA standards. Experience leading HSSE teams and building a hands-on, field-credible safety culture across a distributed, multi-site network. Proven ability to work across matrixed reporting lines while maintaining clear accountability and independence of judgement. Strong incident investigation, risk assessment and corrective action experience. Bachelor's degree in occupational safety, environmental science, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered. Who You Will Work With You'll work with bp's central HSSE function, Operations, Construction & Maintenance, Store Support Organizations, and Legal/Compliance. We believe that our team is strengthened by diversity. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment in which everyone is respected and treated fairly. linkedin_detail_4469110683.description: Since 2012, Khazna has become the leading wholesale data center provider in the Middle East and North Africa, delivering reliable and scalable infrastructure to support the region’s growing digital ecosystem. As part of our Emiratisation initiative, we are seeking an HSE Engineer responsible for ensuring a safe and compliant work environment across all project sites. The role involves reviewing, evaluating, and implementing safety programs and procedures to prevent accidents, injuries, and occupational hazards. The HSE Engineer conducts regular inspections, monitors compliance with HSE regulations, and promotes a strong safety culture in line with company and legal standards. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES: Implement, and monitor HSE plans, policies, and procedures in line with project and regulatory requirements. Conduct risk assessments, Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs), and implement control measures to eliminate or minimize hazards. Inspect project sites, equipment, and work practices to ensure compliance with safety standards and engineering specifications. Lead incident investigations, identify root causes, and recommend corrective and preventive actions. Provide HSE induction and technical training to employees, contractors, and site personnel. Ensure proper handling, storage, and disposal of materials and hazardous substances. Review and update HSE documentation in accordance with current legislation and standards (e.g., ISO 45001, local authority codes). Maintain accurate HSE records, permits, and compliance reports for audits and management review. Stop and report any unsafe activities or conditions, promoting a proactive safety culture across all project phases. QUALIFICATIONS & COMPETENCIES: Bachelor’s degree in safety management, engineering or a relevant field is preferred. Certificate in occupational health and safety 5 plus years of proven experience in Health and Safety in GCC Region Proven experience as Health Safety Officer In depth knowledge of legislation (e.g. NEBOSH, OSHS, OSHA) and procedures Knowledge of potentially hazardous materials or practices Experience in writing reports and policies for health and safety Familiarity with conducting data analysis and reporting statistics Proficient in MS Office; working knowledge of safety management information systems is a plus.

linkedin_detail_4473967458.description: Remote (U.S.) — Full Time The Cari Network is building a blockchain-based payment system powering real-time, 24/7 movement of digital money across the traditional finance and digital asset ecosystems. A pre-launch startup, we're creating an entirely new category of financial infrastructure that brings cash on chain through tokenization while powering the full spectrum of payments for our network—banks, digital asset exchanges, and, most importantly, the customers they serve. About The Role You'll work within the systems that take a payment instruction and turn it into an immutable, on-chain record—implementing features and extensions within an established transaction pipeline architecture, alongside senior engineers who own its design. That means building out pieces of the integration layer between our backend services and our institutional custody platform, and contributing to transaction integrity from calldata construction through on-chain finality on our private ZKsync-based L2. You'll also work directly in our smart contract suite, extending existing contracts under established upgrade-safety and role-governance patterns, and building the audit trail and compliance evidence that regulated bank partners require. What You'll Do Implement components of the transaction lifecycle: calldata construction, custody platform signing requests, nonce handling, L2 submission, and finality confirmation, working within the pipeline architecture senior engineers on the team have designed Build features within the signing pipeline—new submission paths, throughput handling against custody platform rate limits, async transaction submission logic—under existing architectural patterns Implement payment integrity controls: commitment hash verification at pipeline handoff points and co-signer policy evaluation logic Extend our Solidity smart contracts, following established upgrade-safety, storage-layout, and role-governance conventions Contribute to the custody platform authorization policy integration and co-signer agent for custodian-owned transaction authorization Build structured audit trail logging from transaction origination through on-chain execution, satisfying evidentiary requirements for bank partners under regulatory oversight Contribute to the async transaction queue supporting tiered SLAs and per-bank throughput quotas Write high-coverage tests across backend services and smart contracts, maintaining our coverage threshold Participate in on-call, working through known issue patterns independently and escalating novel failure modes to senior engineers Qualifications 3–5 years of backend software engineering experience, with 1–2 years working directly on EVM-compatible blockchain systems Solid proficiency in TypeScript; familiarity with Effect (effect.ts) or a comparable functional effect system is a plus Working familiarity with EVM transaction mechanics: ABI encoding, nonce management, gas estimation, revert handling, and event decoding Some production experience with Solidity smart contract development, including exposure to upgradeable proxy patterns (UUPS) and OpenZeppelin contract libraries Exposure to institutional custody or key management APIs is a strong plus, though not required Understanding of idempotency, at-least-once delivery, and crash recovery concepts in async systems Comfortable asking for help extending existing patterns while building toward independent ownership of larger features Nice to Haves Experience with ZKsync or ZK Stack-based chains—particularly developer-facing constraints like calldata handling, system contract interactions, and AA transaction formats Familiarity with Kafka or message-queue-backed async pipelines Prior work in fintech, payments, or any regulated financial infrastructure environment Foundry proficiency (forge test, forge fmt) What We Offer Competitive compensation Remote-first work environment Opportunity to shape a market-defining protocol with an experienced founding team Meaningful influence over product design at the earliest stage Interested in this role? Send us your resume. ‹ Senior Data Engineer Senior Blockchain Engineer ›

linkedin_detail_4472502259.description: Company Description Entertainment Finance Summit is an annual global capital marketplace that connects the entertainment industry with investors, financial expertise, and strategic capital solutions. The Summit convenes family offices, private equity professionals, financiers, producers, studios, distributors, advisors, and other leaders to explore the evolving business of entertainment finance. Its focus spans film and television finance, media investment, production funding, entertainment funds, private capital, intellectual property, distribution, and tax-advantaged structures. Through summits, curated networking, educational programming, investor discussions, and dealmaking opportunities, Entertainment Finance Summit helps entertainment ventures access smart capital and enables capital providers to understand the entertainment economy. The event is designed for people and institutions shaping the future of entertainment finance and real-world asset innovation. Role Description The Real World Asset Tokenization Specialist will support the design and implementation of tokenization strategies for entertainment-related assets, with a focus on film, television, and media projects. This contract, hybrid role is based in Zurich, with a combination of on-site collaboration and work-from-home flexibility to accommodate project and event schedules. Day-to-day responsibilities include analyzing entertainment assets for tokenization suitability, mapping legal, regulatory, and financial structures, and collaborating with legal, tax, and compliance experts to ensure robust frameworks. The specialist will help design token models, support the creation of offering and investor materials, and coordinate with technology partners on token issuance and lifecycle management. The role also involves market research on digital asset trends, engaging with investors and industry stakeholders, and contributing to panels, workshops, and educational content related to tokenized entertainment finance. Qualifications Strong understanding of real-world asset tokenization, digital securities structures, and token economics. Experience in entertainment finance, media investment, or structured finance for film, television, or related assets. Knowledge of relevant regulatory and compliance frameworks (e.g., securities regulation, KYC/AML, cross-border investment considerations). Ability to collaborate with legal, tax, and technical teams to design compliant tokenization structures and documentation. Familiarity with blockchain platforms, smart contracts, and digital asset infrastructure used for issuing and managing tokenized assets. Strong analytical, research, and financial modeling skills, with the ability to assess risk, return, and capital structure options. Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills for investor materials, presentations, and educational content. Proven ability to work in a hybrid environment in Zurich, manage multiple projects, and engage professionally with global stakeholders. Bachelor’s or master’s degree in finance, economics, law, business, or a related field; experience with private equity or venture capital is an advantage. linkedin_detail_4472695498.description: FUNDRAISING CHAIRPERSON – PROJECT FINANCE & INTERNATIONAL CAPITAL Location: Dubai, UAE Project Focus: Indian Companies & Projects Working Model: Hybrid Position Level: Senior Leadership / Chairperson Benefits: Salary + Equity + Performance-Based Benefits Company & Project Description BLACKBULL LAW HOUSE, a corporate legal and LegalTech organization working in coordination with the BLACKBULL Chamber of Investment, is developing a new Dubai-based platform focused on international fundraising, project finance, institutional collaboration, LegalTech, legal-finance infrastructure, and business development for Indian companies and projects. BLACKBULL is seeking an experienced Fundraising Chairperson capable of establishing a strong Dubai-based investor and institutional network and developing structured financing channels for eligible Indian businesses, assets, and projects. The broader initiative also includes development of LegalTech, new banking and financial channels, an Indian NBFC ecosystem, legal training programs and institutions, and an international project-development platform for Indian businesses and professionals. A significant initial mandate includes supporting BLACKBULL's targeted fundraising requirement of approximately USD 25 million, alongside development of financing channels for selected Indian corporate projects. Role Description The Fundraising Chairperson – Project Finance & International Capital will lead BLACKBULL's fundraising and institutional relationship strategy from Dubai. This is not a conventional advisory or administrative position. The selected professional must have practical fundraising capabilities, credible investor relationships, project-finance expertise, and the ability to progress transactions from initial opportunity through financial closure. The Chairperson will establish relationships with: - Family offices and HNW/UHNW investors - Private equity and private credit funds - Investment companies and asset managers - Banks and financial institutions - Development and institutional finance organizations - Corporate investment groups - Strategic investors and co-investment partners - International project-finance and structured-finance providers Key Responsibilities The Fundraising Chairperson will be responsible for developing a Dubai–India capital corridor for qualified Indian projects. Responsibilities include originating and arranging project finance, growth capital, acquisition finance, structured finance, private credit, strategic investment, equity capital, and other commercially appropriate funding structures. The Chairperson will identify international investors and institutions capable of financing Indian businesses and coordinate investor presentations, financial modelling, valuations, due diligence, negotiations, term sheets, transaction structuring, documentation, and financial closure. The role also requires developing international relationships and collaborations that can provide recurring institutional capital rather than one-time funding arrangements. Indian Asset-Backed Financing Development A major objective is to explore financing solutions for qualified Indian companies supported by Indian commercial properties, business assets, operating cash flows, receivables, contracts, enterprise value, or other acceptable security. For suitable transactions, BLACKBULL intends to explore financing requirements of up to approximately 40% of independently assessed eligible asset/property value. This percentage is a target transaction parameter and not a guaranteed LTV or financing commitment. Every transaction will remain subject to independent valuation, lender/investor underwriting, security enforceability, due diligence, commercial viability, regulatory requirements, and final approval. Depending upon the transaction and applicable legal framework, investment structures may involve: Interest/finance returns | Equity participation | Profit sharing | Revenue participation | Strategic investment | Structured credit | Co-investment NBFC & New Banking Channel Development The Chairperson will also support BLACKBULL's proposed development of a new NBFC and institutional financial ecosystem in India. Responsibilities may include identifying potential: - NBFC acquisition or strategic participation opportunities - Institutional funding alliances - Banking and lending partnerships - Private credit relationships - Co-lending or eligible financial partnerships - Technology and LegalTech integrations - Corporate funding channels - Investor and financial-institution collaborations The objective is to establish a sustainable financial network capable of supporting Indian businesses through appropriately regulated structures. Dubai Capital Platform Dubai will operate as the principal international fundraising, investor-relations, institutional networking, transaction-coordination, and capital-development centre for the project. The Chairperson will explore lawful structures through which eligible Indian businesses and assets can attract international capital while maintaining appropriate investor protections, financial reporting, governance, transaction controls, and regulatory compliance. linkedin_detail_4475547338.description: Job description: Job Title: Assistant Service Manager. Company: SAS- Toyota Dealer. Location: Erbil. Overall Objective of the Job: The Assistant Service Manager will provide essential support to the service manager in overseeing the daily operations of the service department in the branch and will assist in managing daily operations, coordinating service activities, and ensuring the delivery of exceptional customer service in the service center. Tasks and Responsibilities: Participates in establishing the Service Department's long- and short-term objectives, cascading them at the branch level, and communicating them to subordinates, ensuring high-quality achievement of goals in a cost-effective and timely manner. Supervises the activities of subordinates to ensure their effectiveness and compliance with the Company's approved policies and procedures. Selects, trains, motivates, evaluates, and develops branch service personnel to ensure the achievement of SAS objectives. Keeps abreast of developments and new technologies, adopting best international practices in the workplace. Manages service operations performance, including reception and customer handling, completing necessary procedures for vehicle entrance, and establishing proper maintenance schedules. Approves vehicle maintenance requirements after reviewing and analyzing detailed maintenance reports. Ensures the service team within the branch follows up with customers to update them on any progress or delays. Ensures all information regarding service functions within the branch is well-documented and filed, relevant reports are issued on time, and any deviations are reported with corrective action taken. Conducts at least one random car inspection and road test per week to ensure high levels of quality are maintained. Manages the workshop/body shop within the branch, ensuring compliance with SAS's procedures and maintaining professional and efficient service levels. Supports service teams within the branch in acquiring the best possible tools and technologies to perform up to global standards. Prepares periodic reports on vehicle performance and customer feedback. Coordinates with Sales and Marketing Department, Training Manager, and Spare Parts Department to ensure adequate cooperation and smooth workflow between departments. Communicates with the CRM section to receive customer feedback or complaints and conducts customer satisfaction surveys. Follows up on warranty issues and ensures accurate claims submission to insurance and manufacturers. Ensures proper billing and collection of payments are followed up on. Maintains excellent workshop and body shop conditions by monitoring cleanliness and display within the branch. Reviews customer invoices within the branch, ensuring accuracy in line with SARDAR's Policies and Procedures. Communicates with customers to determine the level of performance of maintenance works and follows up to resolve complaints efficiently. Monitors and ensures high safety and security standards are implemented within the branch, managing service buildings, tools, and equipment in optimum condition. Job Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering/ Auto Engineering or a related major. Minimum 7 years of experience in a related field. Minimum 2 years of experience in a managerial position. Strong knowledge of vehicle diagnostics, repair processes, maintenance procedures, and manufacturer service standards. Good understanding of warranty procedures, service KPIs, workshop productivity, and customer satisfaction metrics. Strong leadership and people management skills with the ability to motivate and support a service team. Ability to plan and coordinate workshop operations while ensuring timely vehicle delivery. Excellent communication, customer service, and conflict resolution skills. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint). Ability to work under pressure, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines. Valid driving license. Fluent in English; Arabic and Kurdish language skills are an advantage.

linkedin_detail_4475560330.description: Remote (U.S.) — Full Time The Cari Network is building a blockchain-based payment system powering real-time, 24/7 movement of digital money across the traditional finance and digital asset ecosystems. A pre-launch startup, we’re creating an entirely new category of financial infrastructure that brings cash on chain through tokenization while powering the full spectrum of payments for our network—banks, digital asset exchanges, and, most importantly, the customers they serve. About The Role You'll own the systems that take a payment instruction and turn it into an immutable, on-chain record—as the trusted technical decision-maker for that domain. That means designing and extending the integration layer between our backend services and our institutional custody platform, and being accountable for transaction integrity from calldata construction through on-chain finality on our private ZKsync-based L2. You'll also own significant parts of our smart contract suite, maintaining upgrade safety, on-chain event integrity, and audit trails that satisfy the compliance and evidentiary requirements of regulated bank partners. What You'll Do Own the end-to-end transaction lifecycle as a domain: calldata construction, custody platform signing requests, nonce management, L2 submission, and finality confirmation Design the signing pipeline architecture — parallelization strategies, throughput management against custody platform rate limits, and async transaction submission patterns — and write the RFCs other engineers build against Define what production-ready means for the signing pipeline: alerting thresholds, runbooks, and SLOs, and lead incident response and root-causing when it falls short Build and maintain payment integrity controls: commitment hash verification at pipeline handoff points and co-signer policy evaluation to prevent tampering between transaction origination and on-chain execution Extend and harden our Solidity smart contracts with a focus on upgrade safety, storage layout discipline, and role governance Develop and maintain the custody platform authorization policy integration and co-signer agent for custodian-owned transaction authorization Implement structured audit trails from transaction origination through on-chain execution, satisfying evidentiary requirements for bank partners under regulatory oversight Drive the design of the async transaction queue, enabling tiered SLAs and per-bank throughput quotas at scale Mentor engineers earlier in their blockchain careers, and be the team's go-to for EVM transaction mechanics and custody integration questions Push back on scope or timeline with technical reasoning when a proposed change puts pipeline correctness at risk Qualifications 5–7 years of backend software engineering experience, with at least 3 years working directly on EVM-compatible blockchain systems Strong proficiency in TypeScript; experience with Effect (effect.ts) or a comparable functional effect system is highly valued Deep familiarity with EVM transaction mechanics: ABI encoding, nonce management, gas estimation, revert handling, and event decoding Production experience with Solidity smart contract development, including upgradeable proxy patterns (UUPS preferred) and OpenZeppelin contract libraries Experience integrating with institutional custody or key management APIs Understanding of MPC signing infrastructure and the operational model of custodial signing pipelines Strong instincts around financial-grade reliability: idempotency, at-least-once delivery, crash recovery, and reconciliation in async transaction systems Comfortable owning a domain independently and writing design docs that other engineers act on without you in the room Nice to Haves Experience with ZKsync or ZK Stack-based chains — particularly developer-facing constraints like calldata handling, system contract interactions, and AA transaction formats Familiarity with Kafka or message-queue-backed async signing pipelines Prior work in fintech, payments, or any regulated financial infrastructure environment Experience building or operating blockchain event indexers or transaction monitors Foundry proficiency (forge test, forge fmt, Foundry Upgrades for storage layout validation) Experience mentoring junior engineers What We Offer Competitive compensation: salary, bonus, and equity Full medical, vision, dental benefits 401(k) with matching program Flexible vacation policy (PTO) and remote-first work environment Interested in this role? Send us your resume. ‹ Blockchain Engineer

linkedin_detail_4473647795.description: Organizational Setting The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) in Iraq supports the Government of Iraq in strengthening food security, sustainable agriculture, resilient livelihoods and rural development. FAO works in close collaboration with national and local authorities, farming communities and other relevant stakeholders to implement programmes responding to the priorities of the agriculture sector. The position is based in Karbala and will support the field-level implementation of FAO agricultural activities in the governorate, with particular focus on date palm production systems and support to farmers. The incumbent will work closely with the FAO technical team, relevant government counterparts, local stakeholders and beneficiaries to facilitate the effective implementation and monitoring of project activities at field level. Reporting Lines The Technical Project Assistant will work under the direct supervision of the FAO representative in Iraq and in close coordination with FAO technical teams. Technical Focus Support implementation of agricultural activities including crop management, integrated pest management (IPM), post-harvest practices, farmer field schools (FFS), and project data management, with a focus on date palm and related value chains. Tasks And Responsibilities Support the technical team in meetings, workshops, and conferences Assist in crop management and application of Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) in farmers’ orchards Support crop protection and Integrated Pest Management (IPM) activities Assist in post-harvest treatments, processing, and marketing activities Contribute to the preparation of technical documents and training materials Organize logistical arrangements for trainings, events, and field visits Handle travel arrangements for project teams and counterparts Maintain and organize office files, records, and documentation Liaise with Farmer Field School (FFS) facilitators and support field implementation Collect, organize, and monitor field data Consolidate reports from FFS facilitators and Survey123 platform Analyze field data and prepare assessment reports Maintain records of equipment distribution and warehouse inventories Support preparation of communication materials Prepare periodic activity reports CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING Minimum Requirements University degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Plant Protection, or related field Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in agricultural field projects Working knowledge of Arabic National of Iraq or resident of the country with a valid work permit. linkedin_detail_4476342534.description: This role is a full-time engagement with the client, fully remote. Open to LATAM, USA & Canada. The Mission Help build and scale the secure on-chain infrastructure powering the next generation of open finance. In this role, you’ll design, implement, and battle-test critical smart contracts that manage significant TVL and capital-efficient primitives. This isn't about deploying speculative tokens; it’s about constructing highly resilient, mathematical, and adversarial-resistant software that remains upgradeable, cost-efficient, and bulletproof over time. The Role As a core protocol contributor, you will take deep ownership of smart contract architecture from initial mathematical modeling and design through to mainnet deployment, external audit facilitation, and live monitoring. • Protocol Architecture (40%): Design and implement secure, gas-optimized Solidity smart contracts for lending, borrowing, vaults, yield routing, liquidations, and access control. • Testing & Simulation (30%): Write extensive unit, integration, fork, fuzz, and invariant tests utilizing modern frameworks to ensure zero-day resiliency. • Security & Audits (15%): Prepare codebases for top-tier external audits, remediate findings, and design proactive on-chain risk mitigation/monitoring strategies. • Cross-Functional Integration (15%): Collaborate closely with risk, frontend, indexer, and quantitative engineering teams to build seamless, secure end-to-end dApps. The Must-Haves • Experience: 4+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 2+ years writing, deploying, and maintaining highly secure Solidity smart contracts in production.. • Tooling & Frameworks: Expert-level mastery of Foundry (Forge, Cast) including advanced fuzzing, invariant testing, and mainnet fork simulations. • EVM Deep Dive: Thorough understanding of EVM internals, storage layouts, gas optimization strategies, assembly (Yul), and standard proxy/upgradeability patterns. • DeFi Primitives: Practical, working knowledge of core financial primitives (such as ERC-20/4626/721/1155, AMMs, lending pools, oracles, and liquidation engines). • AI-Assisted Acceleration: Comfort using modern AI coding tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude, Copilot) to accelerate unit testing, documentation, and boilerplate development, backed by the critical judgment required never to trust raw model outputs blindly. • Security Mindset: An obsessive awareness of common attack vectors (reentrancy, oracle manipulation, front-running, rounding errors, and access-control flaws). The Bonus Skills • Audit Pedigree: Prior experience guiding a protocol through a major external audit (e.g., Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin, Spearbit) or participating in competitive security audits. • Multi-Chain/SVM: Exposure to Rust-based smart contract environments (SVM/Solana, CosmWasm) or zero-knowledge (ZK) rollup architectures. • Advanced Automation: Familiarity with off-chain automation infrastructure like Keepers, Defender, or Gelato. Personal Traits • Adversarial Thinker: You don't just think about how code should work; you instinctively try to find ways to break, front-run, or exploit the state machine you are building.. • Execution & Ownership: You act as an owner, not a ticket executor. You proactively trace edge cases, optimize gas, and address technical debt before it is flagged.. • Detail-Obsessed: You care about the nuance of a single uint256 math operation and understand why rounding down vs. up is a security-critical decision.. • Collaborative & Clear: You can distill complex cryptographic or financial system logic into clear documentation and explain architectural tradeoffs to non-smart contract engineers.. Location: Remote (with meaningful overlap with US/EU working hours)

linkedin_detail_4476719634.description: Job Description Job Description About D3 D3 is building the world's first purpose-built blockchain for DomainFi —bringing domain tokenization and DeFi primitives to a massive, rapidly growing $350B+ real-world asset class . We're revolutionizing how existing and future domain names are owned, traded, and leveraged in the digital economy. Our elite team is stacked with industry veterans who have spent the last three decades shaping the internet , from pioneering domain name monetization to architecting key internet protocols to launching and running major TLDs like .xyz, .inc, .tv, and .link . With a proven track record of innovation and success, we're now redefining what's possible in the domain space. We recently closed a $25M Series A led by Paradigm - one of the best investors in the industry. This will help fuel our mission to bring domains fully on-chain and unlock new financial possibilities for one of the internet's most valuable asset classes. We're based in Los Angeles, with team members all over the world. We're looking for driven, talented builders to help build a trillion-dollar DomainFi economy. Join us! Job Overview We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Solana Blockchain Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will work on the design and implementation of our DOMA Protocol connecting traditional DNS and web3 naming technologies to create a unified naming system compatible across the Internet and all blockchains. You will play a critical role in developing and maintaining our core platform APIs and smart contracts integration with the Solana blockchain. Familiarity with Solana smart contracts and blockchain standards such as SPL Token, Metaplex, and Token-2022 is essential. Key Responsibilities Collaborate with the product team to understand requirements and translate them into technical specifications and features. Lead the research, design, implementation, deployment and monitoring of the DOMA Protocol that enables tokenization of domains as Real World Assets (RWAs) onto the Solana blockchain. Research, implement and maintain Solana programs to enable "DomainFi" applications across the Solana ecosystem. This includes tokenization, name resolution, secondary trading, and lending/borrowing. Implement backend services to interface with the Solana blockchain and traditional DNS Registry/Registrar infrastructure. Ensure the scalability, performance, and security of the protocol and application. Ensure code quality through code reviews, testing, and debugging. Maintain and optimize the performance of existing codebase and address any bugs or issues that arise. Stay up-to-date with the latest technologies, frameworks, and best practices in web development, blockchain, and smart contract development. Qualifications Strong passion for Blockchain technologies and protocols. Extensive knowledge and experience in Solana blockchain including smart contract development and deployment, blockchain bridges, oracles, indexers, decentralized finance, and NFT marketplaces. Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related field. Relevant certifications and additional coursework are a plus. Minimum 5 years of professional experience in backend development using Node.js and MySQL/Postgres. Minimum 3 years experience in blockchain development using Solidity/Rust, with strong understanding of distributed systems, consensus algorithms and storage subsystems. Familiarity with Git version control and Agile methodologies for collaborative development. Strong problem-solving skills, adaptability, and a self-motivated attitude, with a willingness to learn new technologies in a fast-paced startup environment. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and within cross-functional teams to achieve business goals. Pluses DevOps experience with Kubernetes, Digital Ocean, Google Cloud, AWS, and Linux environments. Familiarity with NestJS and GraphQL. Have prior experience maintaining or creating blockchain oracles. Why D3, Why Now? Ground-Floor Growth, Learning, and Impact : D3 is your chance to dive headfirst into an ultra-early-stage company where every move you make truly matters. You'll have the opportunity to sharpen your skills, expand your expertise, and shape the foundation of something groundbreaking. Almost everything we're building today at D3 is "zero-to-one," meaning you'll be among the first to craft, refine, and launch key initiatives that define our future success. Strong, Proven Leadership : At D3, you'll work alongside industry visionaries who have been there, done that, and are ready to do it again—only bigger. Our leadership team brings veteran industry experience, sharp insights, and a relentless drive to do big things across every function at D3. You'll gain invaluable mentorship, develop a high-impact mindset, and be challenged to grow in ways you never imagined. Unique Market Positioning – We're pioneering at the intersection of internet infrastructure, real-world assets, and blockchain communities, creating solutions that redefine what's possible in Web3. If you want to push boundaries, solve complex problems, and be part of a team that's shaping the future of the Internet, D3 is the place to do it.

Conducting risk assessments to identify potential hazards and developing preventative strategies. Organizing safety training for employees to ensure awareness and understanding of safety and environmental practices and legislation. Monitoring compliance with policies, performing site inspections, and preparing detailed reports on findings. Leading emergency response initiatives and conducting investigations after incidents to establish causes and preventive measures. Strong understanding of the legal health and safety guidelines relevant to the industry. Several years of experience in a HSE role, ideally within the industry or a closely related field. Proficient use of HSE management software and tools. What We Offer: Opportunity to work on strategically important Oil & Gas projects. International and multicultural working environment. Competitive compensation package. Professional growth and leadership opportunities within a dynamic project organization.

linkedin_detail_4475218825.description: Role Description The Blockchain Engineer / Blockchain Architect / Crypto Specialist develops and supports blockchain technologies and digital asset solutions. Depending on the assigned specialization, the role involves building blockchain applications and integrations, designing system architectures, or analyzing crypto assets, protocols, and ecosystem developments. The successful candidate will collaborate with engineering, product, security, finance, and compliance teams to evaluate requirements and deliver reliable solutions. This position also assesses technical and operational risks, validates system behavior or research findings, and maintains clear documentation. Architecture responsibilities may include defining technical standards and guiding implementation across teams. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, finance, economics, mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant experience in blockchain engineering, solution architecture, digital assets, or crypto research. Understanding of blockchain networks, consensus mechanisms, smart contracts, wallets, and transaction lifecycles. For engineering positions, proficiency in languages such as Solidity, Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript, with experience developing and testing blockchain applications. For architect positions, demonstrated experience designing secure, scalable systems and evaluating interoperability, performance, and governance trade-offs. For crypto specialist positions, knowledge of token economics, digital asset markets, liquidity, custody, and protocol risks. Familiarity with blockchain APIs, node infrastructure, indexing tools, and on-chain analytics. Awareness of smart contract vulnerabilities, key management, access controls, and secure development practices. Ability to evaluate technical documentation, validate assumptions, and communicate research limitations. Familiarity with version control, automated testing, and deployment workflows for technical positions. Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and commitment to confidentiality and professional integrity. Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across technical and business teams. Relevant projects, research, open-source contributions, or professional certifications are an advantage.

linkedin_detail_4474220056.description: Sanabil Studio is a venture builder that blends industry expertise, technology, and startup know-how to turn bold ideas into real businesses. We take concepts from zero to launch, and when a venture proves its potential, we back it with seed funding and hands-on support to help it scale. At Makan, we believe homeownership in Saudi Arabia should be built on real equity, not just rent. Through a rent-to-own model, residents move in with a 10% down payment instead of the 30% banks require, build real equity every year through their rent, and use that accumulated equity to refinance into a standard bank mortgage if they qualify at year five. We are the founding team building Makan from a validated thesis to signed assets, signed investors, and a functioning company, with Sanabil Studio providing the financial model, pre-seed capital, operational backbone, and institutional governance. About The Role We're looking for a highly experienced Capital & Finance Lead to co-found Makan and own the raising, structuring, and financial model of the business end-to-end. This role is responsible for raising debt and equity, structuring the fund and deal mechanics, and owning investor relations from LOI through signed commitment. You'll work closely with a Real Estate & Asset co-founder and the Sanabil Studio Investment Committee to turn a validated model into closed capital and a licensed fund structure. THE ROLE: What you'll own here. Raise and structure debt and equity from funding partners. Own the financial model, calculating ROI and structuring the capital stack the venture needs. Structure term sheets, waterfalls, and fee economics with institutional investors, family offices, or LPs. Own investor relations: pitching, negotiating, and closing capital partners from LOI through signed commitment. Own the regulatory and fund pathway, from SPV to CMA-licensed fund, and all investor reporting. Help define and execute Makan's go-to-market and capital strategy alongside your co-founder. Represent the venture in front of the Sanabil Studio Investment Committee and institutional LPs. Recruit and lead Makan's founding team across commercial, operations, and product functions. THE PROFILE: You're probably a fit if... You have experience raising debt and/or equity for funds, SPVs, or real-asset-backed vehicles as a fund manager, investment banker, or capital markets professional. You have personally structured a term sheet, waterfall, or fee economics for an institutional investor, family office, or LP. You understand how Saudi family offices, capitals, and banks evaluate real-asset-backed paper, and what it takes to close a commitment. You are comfortable building and defending a financial model, and can confidently calculate ROI and structure a capital stack. You have led a fundraising process or capital-raising function before, including investor reporting and governance. You deeply understand the Saudi capital markets and regulatory environment (SAMA, CMA). You are currently based in or willing to relocate to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Saudi Nationals preferred. Bonus: A named anchor LP or family office relationship that could write a meaningful first ticket; experience with sukuk issuance or structured private placements; prior experience working with or inside a venture studio or venture builder. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: Within the first year, you'll... Have closed initial capital commitments from investors or family offices. Have a licensed and functioning fund/SPV structure in place. Have built a financial model and investor reporting rhythm the Investment Committee trusts. Be recognized as a credible representative of the venture in front of institutional LPs. Be working independently with minimal supervision alongside your co-founder.
